target.title: feat(workspaces): add agent-composable Workspaces
target.body:
Related: #101093

Supersedes the stacked implementation in #101094, #101097, and #101098 while preserving @100yenadmin's original product direction and contributor credit.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's Control UI is a fixed dashboard: agents cannot assemble a durable workspace around the task they are doing, expose useful live data, or refine that workspace without a code change and redeploy.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds an opt-in, agent-composable Workspaces surface with tabs, built-in widgets, typed agent tools, guarded commands, and an approval flow for custom widgets. Workspace state and provenance live in SQLite; custom widget code remains a named user artifact, is content-pinned at approval, size-bounded, served with a restrictive CSP, and rendered in a sandboxed iframe.

The integration was rebuilt from the original three-PR stack, rebased onto current `main`, and hardened through repeated source review and live lifecycle checks. The core boundary stays generic: the bundled Workspaces plugin owns persistence, commands, tools, and widget serving, while Control UI consumes the plugin surface.

## User Impact

The bundled Workspaces plugin is disabled by default and can be enabled from the Control UI Plugins page or with `openclaw plugins enable workspaces`. Once enabled, agents can create and refine task-specific workspaces on demand. Users can inspect provenance, reorder and resize widgets, move them across tabs, approve or reject custom widget proposals, and retain the result across sessions without editing JSON or redeploying OpenClaw.

## Evidence

- Live OpenAI proof: an OpenClaw agent using `openai/gpt-5.4` created and refined an `OpenAI Live` workspace with six widgets across five built-in kinds in 46.8 seconds. The resulting workspace persisted in SQLite with no JSON workspace sidecar.
- [Screenshot proof and artifact manifest](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104139#issuecomment-4942481424) show the agent-authored Workspaces surface and widget controls.
- Exact-head sanitized AWS Crabbox proof passed 98 Workspaces plugin tests and the full Control UI unit suite (214 files, 3,280 tests) on public networking with no Tailscale or instance profile, isolated HOME, and pinned Node/pnpm (`run_01f377b15a46`, `run_5a854a2b8b5f`).
- Full `node scripts/build-all.mjs` completed successfully on the feature branch; an earlier full validation covered 285 tests.
- Fresh autoreview iterated through the approval, serving, manifest, binding, and filesystem boundaries until it reported no accepted/actionable findings. A final review after the exact lint fixes was also clean.
- Exact-head CI is rerunning after the generated documentation map refresh.

  • For performance and accuracy reasons, improved incremental analysis will now only be enabled on a pull request when diff-informed analysis is also enabled for that run.   • If multiple inputs are provided for the GitHub-internal analysis-kinds input, only code-scanning will be enabled. The analysis-kinds input is experimental, for GitHub-internal use only, and may change without notice at any time. #3892
  • Added an experimental change which, when running a Code Scanning analysis for a PR with improved incremental analysis enabled, prefers CodeQL CLI versions that have a cached overlay-base database for the configured languages. This speeds up analysis for a repository when there is not yet a cached overlay-base database for the latest CLI version. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in May. #3880

4.35.4 - 07 May 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.4. #3881

4.35.3 - 01 May 2026

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.19.3 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 9 April 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.15, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3837
  • Configurations for private registries that use Cloudsmith or GCP OIDC are now accepted. #3850
  • Best-effort connection tests for private registries now use GET requests instead of HEAD for better compatibility with various registry implementations. For NuGet feeds, the test is now always performed against the service index. #3853
  • Fixed a bug where two diagnostics produced within the same millisecond could overwrite each other on disk, causing one of them to be lost. #3852

target.title: fix(tlon): stop monitor tracking state from growing forever
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Affected surface / workflow: long-running bundled Tlon monitors, including mention-free follow-ups in threads where the bot previously participated and automatic handling of pending DM invitations received from the chat `/v3` stream.

## Why This Change Was Made

### Root cause, in product terms

The monitor kept every participated thread parent and every successfully handled DM-invite ship in process-lifetime `Set`s. Unique identifiers therefore accumulated until restart.

A count-bounded cache is appropriate for thread participation, but not for DM invites: Tlon sends the `/v3` invite array as the complete current pending-invite snapshot. The first snapshot implementation also had an activation race: work started before an invite disappeared could finish after the same ship reappeared and incorrectly mark the new activation processed. Delayed processing from an old multi-key snapshot could likewise adopt a newer activation unless the processor itself was bound to its originating snapshot.

## User Impact

The monitor no longer retains tracking identifiers forever. Active DM invites remain deduplicated even for snapshots larger than 2,000 entries, while an invite that disappears and later reappears is eligible for new RSVP or approval work.

Thread participation is intentionally bounded to the 2,000 most recently used parent IDs. An older evicted thread requires a fresh bot mention before mention-free follow-ups resume. This delivery-window tradeoff remains an explicit Tlon-owner decision rather than being presented as behavior-neutral.

## Fix classification

Root-cause fix.

## Complete shipped solution

- Replace the lifetime participated-thread set with the shared access-refreshed LRU cache, capped at 2,000 entries.
- Treat every `/v3` DM-invite array as the authoritative active snapshot instead of imposing an arbitrary count cap.
- Assign a per-key activation generation: continuously active ships preserve their generation; removal invalidates it; reappearance receives a new generation.
- Coalesce work only for the same ship and generation. Failed or rejected work leaves same-generation waiters able to retry.
- Commit successful work only while the task still owns the active generation.
- Delete in-flight state only when the exact entry object still owns that map slot, so stale cleanup cannot erase newer work.
- Return a snapshot-bound processor from `beginSnapshot()`, preventing delayed work from an old snapshot from adopting a newer generation.

## Why this is a root-cause fix

The ownership boundaries now match the two data sources: thread participation has an explicit bounded recency policy, while DM-invite retention follows the protocol's active snapshot. Generation ownership is checked at both work coalescing and commit time, so stale asynchronous completion cannot mutate the state of a later activation.

## Key design boundary / source of truth

The chat `/v3` array is the source of truth for currently pending DM invites. Tracking state in this patch is process-local and ephemeral; it does not alter a persistent cache schema, configuration schema, public SDK, database, migration, or Tlon wire format.

## Non-goals / what did not change

- No change to invite eligibility, allowlist checks, RSVP payloads, approval payloads, or Urbit transport behavior.
- No persistence or restart recovery was added.
- No group-invite path or unrelated monitor state was refactored.
- No public API or user-facing configuration was added.

## Out-of-scope boundary

The exact thread retention policy is intentionally limited to the existing 2,000-entry proposal. If Tlon ownership prefers a different count or expiry policy, that is a maintainer product decision; the invite generation fix is independent of that choice.

## Related open PR scan

No linked issue or competing canonical PR was identified by the existing-PR workflow. The patch remains limited to the four Tlon monitor implementation/test files.

## Evidence

### Targeted regression tests

Focused Vitest run:

```text
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests       8 passed (8)
```

Coverage includes:

- LRU eviction and recency refresh.
- 2,001 participated threads, proving only the retained recent parent accepts an unmentioned follow-up.
- Active invite snapshots larger than 2,000 entries without replay thrashing.
- Removal and reappearance while old work remains in flight.
- New-generation work starting before stale work settles.
- Same-generation coalescing and retry after false or rejection.
- Exact-entry cleanup preserving newer in-flight work.
- Delayed old-snapshot work being rejected instead of adopting a new generation.

## Test scenario / real behavior proof

An exact-head loopback fixture ran production `monitorTlonProvider()` with the real `UrbitSSEClient`. It accepted real HTTP channel PUTs and emitted SSE `/v3` snapshots. The fixture blocked generation A's RSVP, removed and re-added the invite, started generation C before A settled, verified same-generation coalescing and stale-cleanup fencing, failed C once, and observed a retry.

```text
command: production monitorTlonProvider + real UrbitSSEClient loopback fixture
head: 38a7443490f005f0fa5f622db3a72be1f7a15f35
main_base: b7156ce68884b9c6bf523f9db40da97bad0776ba
fixture_transport: real HTTP channel PUTs and SSE /v3 snapshots
old_generation_attempt_started: true
remove_then_readd_before_old_settled: true
new_generation_started_before_old_settled: true
same_generation_waiter_coalesced: true
stale_cleanup_preserved_current_inflight: true
current_generation_failed_once_then_retried: true
total_rsvp_attempts: 3
runtime_errors_expected: 1
assertions: PASS
exit_code: 0
```

The fixture used loopback HTTP only and no external Tlon account or endpoint.

## Additional verification

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test` — passed.
- `pnpm format:check -- extensions/tlon/src/monitor/index.ts extensions/tlon/src/monitor/tracking.ts extensions/tlon/src/monitor/tracking.test.ts extensions/tlon/src/monitor/index.tracking.test.ts` — passed.
- Targeted `oxlint` on all four changed files — 0 warnings, 0 errors.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- `pnpm check:changed -- extensions/tlon/src/monitor/index.ts extensions/tlon/src/monitor/tracking.ts extensions/tlon/src/monitor/tracking.test.ts extensions/tlon/src/monitor/index.tracking.test.ts` — attempted, but the local command delegates to Blacksmith Testbox and the installed Crabbox binary failed its basic `--version`/`--help` sanity check before running remote lanes. The focused tests, extension test typecheck, format, lint, and diff checks above were run locally instead.

The local machine uses Node 22.17, below the repository's Node 22.19+ floor. Focused Vitest runs used a temporary copy of the repository runner that only replaces the unsupported `import.meta.main` entry guard; repository project selection and Vitest configuration were unchanged. The temporary runner and live-proof test were removed after execution.

## Review findings addressed, if any

- **RF-001 — waiting on author:** generation repair, regressions, exact-head proof, and updated explanation are now supplied; label reevaluation remains remote.
- **RF-002 — removal/re-add before original settles:** fixed in helper and monitor-path regressions.
- **RF-003 — 2,000-thread delivery window:** explicitly retained as a Tlon-owner/maintainer decision, not claimed resolved.
- **RF-004 / RF-005 — generation-aware completion:** fixed with activation generations, snapshot-bound processors, and identity-checked cleanup.
- **RF-006 — focused tests:** passed, 2 files / 8 tests.
- **RF-007 — `check:changed`:** attempted; blocked before remote execution by unavailable local Crabbox/Testbox tooling, disclosed above with equivalent local lanes.
- **RF-008 — formatting:** passed.
- **RF-009 — diff check:** passed.

## Regression guardrail

The helper and production-monitor-path tests encode the A/B/C race directly: A starts, B removes the invite, C re-adds it before A settles, and C must run independently. They also verify that A's success and cleanup cannot mark C processed or delete C's in-flight entry, and that C can retry after failure.

## Maintainer readiness summary

- **Affected surface / workflow:** bundled Tlon monitor thread-follow-up eligibility and DM-invite handling from chat `/v3` snapshots.
- **Root cause, in product terms:** the lifecycle root cause was process-lifetime sets retaining every unique thread parent and handled invite; the first snapshot tracker also violated generation state ownership by letting stale async work commit into a later remove/re-add activation.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** tracking memory is now bounded or snapshot-scoped, and a reappeared invite cannot be silently suppressed by stale completion.
- **Fix classification:** root-cause fix.
- **Complete shipped solution:** bounded access-refreshed thread LRU plus authoritative invite snapshots, per-key activation generations, same-generation coalescing/retry, snapshot-bound processors, and identity-checked in-flight cleanup.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** state lifetime now follows the owning source and async results can commit only to the activation in which they started.
- **Key design boundary / source of truth:** the source-of-truth contract is the authoritative `/v3` active DM-invite snapshot; all new tracking is process-local ephemeral state.
- **Non-goals / what did not change:** only monitor-local identifier ownership changed; wire format, RSVP/approval payloads, allowlists, persistence, public API, configuration, migration, and group invites are unchanged, with no unrelated refactor.
- **Compatibility, merge-risk, or maintainer-decision notes:** invite behavior is compatibility-preserving except that correct work now occurs after remove/re-add; the 2,000-thread mention-free window is an intentional message-delivery policy requiring Tlon-owner acceptance.
- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk: message-delivery`; availability and security-boundary signals were reviewed, but no network permission, credential, persistence, or external security boundary changed.
- **Risk explanation:** evicted old thread parents no longer qualify for unmentioned follow-ups until a new mention; generation fencing prevents stale invite work from dropping a new activation.
- **Why acceptable:** the thread cap matches the existing Tlon processed-message window and is explicit for owner review; the invite fix follows the protocol snapshot contract and removes a demonstrated race.
- **Users/operators/developers can now:** run a long-lived Tlon monitor without lifetime growth in these identifier collections and rely on reappeared invites receiving current-generation work.
- **Existing behavior preserved:** current thread entries refresh on use; continuously active invites remain deduplicated; allowlist, owner, approval, logging, and RSVP behavior are unchanged.
- **What was not tested or remains unavailable:** no external Tlon account was used, and repository `check:changed` could not reach Blacksmith Testbox because the installed Crabbox binary failed its local sanity check; equivalent local lanes and a real loopback HTTP/SSE protocol fixture were run.
- **Environment:** Windows, Node v22.17.0, pnpm 11.2.2; the repository requires Node 22.19+, so only the unsupported `import.meta.main` runner guard was replaced in a temporary test-runner copy.
- **Commands run after this patch:** focused repository-selected Vitest; `pnpm tsgo:extensions:test`; targeted `pnpm format:check`; targeted `pnpm exec oxlint`; `git diff --check`; production-monitor loopback HTTP/SSE proof; attempted full `pnpm check:changed` command listed above.
- **Key results / observations:** 2 focused files and 8 tests passed; extension test typecheck, format, lint, and diff checks passed; live proof observed three RSVP attempts with independent new-generation start, same-generation coalescing, stale-cleanup fencing, one expected failure, and successful retry.
- **Review findings addressed, if any:** RF-002 and RF-004 through RF-006 plus RF-008 and RF-009 are fixed/proven; RF-007 is disclosed as an external local-tooling limitation; RF-001 awaits remote reevaluation; RF-003 remains an explicit maintainer decision.
- **Regression guardrail:** the focused regression test and monitor-path integration test encode A-starts/B-removes/C-re-adds-before-A-settles, then assert C starts independently, A cannot commit or clean up C, and C retries after failure.
- **Patch quality notes:** added 10-second `vi.waitFor` limits only to large deterministic 2,001-item monitor tests to avoid default-timeout flakes on slower runners. Existing broad error handling was moved inside the tracked boolean task without widening catches; boolean returns now explicitly represent commit/retry eligibility. No production timeout or retry count changed.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** high for the generation repair and exact-head behavior proof; the only unresolved product choice is acceptance or retuning of the documented 2,000-thread window.

target.title: fix(release): reconcile contribution provenance
target.body:
Closes #103429

> Draft/HOLD: do not merge until the immutable historical reconciliation passes
> on exact signed head `94ff88960d7b52409c4dc9ce75e274fa73f4deac`.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where release maintainers could generate an incomplete
contribution record because the verifier treated first-parent history as the
source inventory and allowed contextual references to stand in for source-PR
ownership.

## Why This Change Was Made

The verifier now inventories the complete raw Git DAG from the unique merge
base, rejects shallow/grafted/replaced history, and assigns each commit through
auditable GitHub associations, strict merged-PR directives, exact/partial/
adapted provenance, verified revert parity, or direct-commit classification.
It records canonical/current/generated/missing/stale sets, compares the
canonical inventory with the complete merged-main GitHub universe, and accepts
only a bounded association-free `CHANGELOG.md` tail after the immutable product
cutoff.

Ledger output is transactional and fail-closed: a pending sentinel replaces any
stale pass before fallible verifier work, output uses sibling temp-file renames,
rollback preserves the pending sentinel, concurrent writers are not overwritten,
and dangling symlink aliases to `CHANGELOG.md` are rejected. Consumers must
verify the current successful invocation plus the actual changelog and release
section hashes; `status: "pass"` alone is not acceptance evidence.

## User Impact

Release maintainers get a deterministic, fail-closed contribution manifest with
complete source-PR credit, direct-commit auditability, explicit
shipped/reverted exclusions, immutable evidence hashes, and concrete
reconciliation metrics before publication.

## Evidence

- Exact signed head: `94ff88960d7b52409c4dc9ce75e274fa73f4deac`.
- Tree: `b588ecba4d358a311a017e6653ddf04568f51e00`.
- Parent: `7af7e41eedf4791202e71ed2cc201732f0659c70`.
- Rebase equivalence: stable patch ID
  `1e917cd19ee77b62130c032289f059bc57c3e8d7`, binary diff SHA-256
  `f746f2311b610f9626a433fe9d9044a716c131d41158bf37745c00d63bca301f`,
  identical before/after rebase; intervening main changes had zero touched-path
  overlap.
- Blacksmith Testbox
  `https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29114961301`, box
  `tbx_01kx6mwcbfvv0hv4nsxe6t4dvf`:
  - exact focused verifier/source-inventory proof: 58/58 passed;
  - broad changed gate: guards, full `tsgo`, core/extensions/scripts oxlint,
    and runtime import-cycle checks passed;
  - exact post-delta `pnpm check:changed --
    test/scripts/verify-release-notes.test.ts`: tooling guards and scripts lint
    passed.
- Fresh structured autoreview: no findings; patch correct, confidence `0.82`.
- Historical fixture model:
  `306b800ace5398dcfc5eae6e15dcae533db42c95` product cutoff to
  `811ddd96180583bae00001f71971419182ae0520` final target, maximum two
  `CHANGELOG.md`-only tail commits. Expected reconciliation:
  `2389 - 421 post-fork - 6 shipped/boundary - 2 reverted = 1960`, with zero
  unclassified PRs. The sole immutable replay is pending on this exact head.

The terminal release-candidate replay intentionally follows landing so the
release branch executes the immutable trusted-main tooling identity. No release
publication is performed by this PR.

target.title: fix: resolve file:// URLs to local paths before saving media
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `createManagedOutgoingImageBlocks` receives a `file://` URL (e.g., from `pathToFileURL(...).href`), `resolveLocalMediaPath` correctly converts it to a local filesystem path for the policy check (`assertLocalMediaAllowed`), but the raw `file://` string was still passed to `saveMediaSource`.

`saveMediaSource` does not recognize the `file://` protocol — only `http://` and `https://` are treated as URLs via `looksLikeUrl()`. The `file://` string falls through to the local file branch, where it attempts to open `"file:///path/to/file"` as a literal filesystem path, causing `createManagedOutgoingImageBlocks` to throw `ManagedImageAttachmentError`.

## Evidence

**Root cause**: The existing code at `managed-image-attachments.ts` already had the correct path resolution via `resolveLocalMediaPath()` for the policy check, but neglected to use the resolved path in the subsequent `saveMediaSource` call.

**Fix**: Changed `saveMediaSource(mediaUrl, ...)` to `saveMediaSource(localMediaPath ?? mediaUrl, ...)`. When `resolveLocalMediaPath` returns a local path (which it does for `file://` URLs via `safeFileURLToPath`), the resolved filesystem path is passed instead of the raw `file://` URL.

**Validation**: The fix is a one-line change at a single call site with a clear logical invariant: if `resolveLocalMediaPath` resolved the source to a local path, that resolved path should be used consistently for both policy checking and media storage.

Fixes #103538

target.title: fix: allow gateway startup when SQLite migration target already exists
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When the shared SQLite state store already contains data from previous migrations, the gateway startup preflight treats informational warnings like `"rows already existed in shared state"` as fatal errors. This causes the gateway to refuse startup with:

```
OpenClaw startup migrations did not complete cleanly; refusing to report the gateway ready.
```

These warnings are informational — they indicate the migration target already exists in SQLite, which is the expected state after a successful prior migration. They should not block gateway startup.

## Evidence

**Fix approach**: Added `partitionMigrationWarnings()` in `doctor-config-preflight.ts` that separates migration warnings into two categories:

- **Informational** (matching patterns like "already existed in shared state", "already has"): These indicate data was already migrated on a previous run and are logged as notices rather than blocking startup.
- **Blocking** (e.g., "Failed migrating...", "Left legacy config health state in place"): These represent real migration failures that should continue to block gateway readiness.

**Test coverage**: Added two new tests that verify:
1. "already existed" warnings allow startup to proceed without throwing
2. Real migration failure warnings (e.g., "Failed migrating...") still block startup

All existing tests continue to pass.

Fixes #103545

target.title: fix(agents): preserve ANSI sanitizer state across bash chunks
target.body:
Closes #103668

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running bash commands through agents could see ANSI/OSC control-sequence fragments leak into streamed tool output, final bash results, and full-output spill files when a process split a terminal sequence across output callbacks.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix adds a reusable incremental ANSI sequence stripper in terminal-core and lets the bash output accumulator use one sanitizer instance for the lifetime of each command. This preserves streaming and bounded-memory behavior while keeping one-shot `stripAnsiSequences()` semantics unchanged for existing callers.

## User Impact

Bash output sanitization is now invariant to callback chunking for OSC and CSI sequences. Agents and users receive the same clean output whether the process emits a complete sequence in one callback or splits it across callbacks.

## Evidence

Before this patch, sanitizing `A\x1b]0;title` and `\x07B` independently leaked fragments such as `Aitle\x07B`; whole-input sanitization returned `AB`.

target.title: feat(ui): add standalone operator approval links
target.body:
Related: #103505

Stacked on #103679. Review this branch from `codex/approval-typed-actions`.

## What Problem This Solves

Approval prompts currently require the operator to remain on the surface that raised them. Even after the durable approval registry and typed channel actions, OpenClaw has no stable, mobile-friendly document that can be opened directly and refreshed to recover canonical approval state.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds a standalone authenticated `${controlUiBasePath}/approve/{approvalId}` Control UI document backed by `approval.get` and `approval.resolve`. The Gateway reserves the one-segment approval namespace before plugins and static-file heuristics, including asset-like IDs, and fails closed with 404 when Control UI serving is disabled.

The document is bound to the Gateway that served it. It does not copy or overwrite the full app's saved remote-Gateway selection; URL/session authentication remains ephemeral until an operator explicitly confirms a different Gateway. Approval IDs are decoded once, credentials never enter the approval URL, and terminal state always comes from the SQLite-backed canonical record.

Resolution returns committed SQLite truth before best-effort channel, push, and legacy-event follow-up. A slow or failed secondary surface therefore cannot delay the winning response or replace its result.

## User Impact

Operators can open a stable approval link on a phone or desktop, authenticate, inspect the sanitized command or plugin preview, and approve or deny. Concurrent answers show `Approved here` on the winner and `Resolved elsewhere` with the recorded canonical decision on losers. Reload, reconnect, expiry, cancellation, malformed data, and unavailable approvals all fail closed without usable decision controls.

## Evidence

- Source-blind built-UI behavior validation passed all 9/9 contract clauses: standalone routing, mounted authentication, exact ID/kind/decision submission, first-answer winner and loser states, terminal reload, fail-closed malformed data, reconnect recovery, dynamic content, 48px mobile targets, no horizontal overflow, and zero browser page/console errors.
- Exact Control UI E2E passed 6/6 scenarios on Testbox, including mobile pending, competing surface, mounted base path, malformed Gateway data, disconnect/reconnect, and content anti-cheat checks.
- Focused Gateway suites passed 430/430 tests; focused UI suites passed 53/53; unified approval handler passed 60/60; UI localization validation passed for all 20 locales.
- Full exact-tree `pnpm check:changed` passed every changed lane, structural guard, typecheck, core/extensions/scripts lint, and runtime import-cycle check in 4m51s ([run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29093807538)).
- Fresh exact-tree structured autoreview found no accepted or actionable findings.
- Final mobile/desktop proof artifacts were generated outside the repository and inspected individually; no screenshots or videos are committed to the product branch.

target.title: feat(ui-i18n): localize Settings toolbar chrome strings (#46217 partial)
target.body:
## Summary

Phase 1 of #46217: replaces 20 hardcoded English strings in the Settings view toolbar with `t()` calls under a new `settings.*` namespace in `ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts`. Runs `pnpm ui:i18n:sync` to regenerate all 18 locale bundles. `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` ship with native-speaker translations (seeded into the TM so they survive future sync runs); other locales fall through to English fallback per the existing no-provider behavior.

Strings covered (toolbar chrome only):
- Mode toggle: `Form`, `Raw`, plus the two toggle tooltips and `Raw mode unavailable for this snapshot`
- Changes badge: `Unsaved changes` (raw mode), `{count} unsaved change` / `{count} unsaved changes` (form mode, sing/plural — fix applied after @clawsweeper review), `No changes`
- Action buttons: `Open`, `Open config file`, `Open {path}` tooltip, `Clear`, `Apply` / `Applying…`, `Update` / `Updating…`
- Search: placeholder, aria-label, clear-search aria-label
- Accordion: `Quick Settings` header
- `Raw mode disabled (snapshot cannot safely round-trip raw text).` notice

The `Save` / `Saving…` button reuses existing `common.save` / `common.saving` keys (which already carry native translations across all locales — `保存` / `保存中…` in zh-CN, `儲存` / `儲存中…` in zh-TW). The sing/plural pair `unsavedChangeCount` / `unsavedChangesCount` follows the repo's existing pattern (`common.checkpoint` / `common.checkpoints`).

## Out of scope (separate PRs to follow)

Per the @clawsweeper review on #46217, the full localization touches three additional surfaces that intentionally are NOT in this PR:

- `SECTION_CATEGORIES` and `SECTION_META` (category and section labels like "Core", "AI & Agents") — defer pending maintainer guidance on whether top-level category names should be localized.
- `src/config/schema.labels.ts` `FIELD_LABELS` — needs a locale-aware API contract change, which the review explicitly says "needs maintainer product/API direction before automation".
- Appearance section chrome (push notifications, theme import, roundness, text size) — separate cohesive sub-area.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Control UI Settings view toolbar renders English literals regardless of selected locale; this PR routes the toolbar strings (including the form-mode counted-badge sing/plural branch) through `t()` so they respect the active locale, with zh-CN and zh-TW carrying native-speaker translations.

Real environment tested: Local macOS arm64 checkout, node v22.22.3, pnpm 11.1.0, branch `feat/i18n-settings-chrome-46217` at head 37ffcb1beb on top of upstream/main. Vite dev server started with `pnpm ui:dev` (port 5173) and a real Chrome browser session loaded the regenerated `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` locale bundles via the running dev server, including the new form-mode count keys added after the @clawsweeper review.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```
pnpm ui:i18n:sync
pnpm ui:i18n:check
pnpm ui:dev
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/i18n/test/translate.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/config.browser.test.ts ui/src/ui/config-form.browser.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/config-form.search.node.test.ts src/config/schema.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs ui/src/i18n/locales/en.ts ui/src/ui/views/config.ts
pnpm tsgo:core
```

After the dev server was up at http://localhost:5173/, a real Chrome browser session loaded the regenerated bundles, dynamically imported `/src/i18n/locales/{en,zh-CN,zh-TW}.ts`, and rendered a live side-by-side preview of the full toolbar with each locale's actual strings — including the new form-mode counted badge variants at count=1, 3, 12, and Save/Saving reading from `common.save` / `common.saving`.

Evidence after fix:

Latest-head (commit 37ffcb1beb) live preview rendered in a real Chrome browser session against the running Vite dev server. Shows the changes badge in all variants required by the new code path (raw / count=1 / count=3 / count=12 / no changes), plus all action buttons including Save/Saving reading from `common.save` / `common.saving`. All three locales side-by-side using the regenerated bundles:

![Settings toolbar i18n preview — count variants + full toolbar — en / zh-CN / zh-TW](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ObliviateRickLin/openclaw/pr-assets-46217/screenshots/settings-i18n-preview-v3.png)

The screenshot shows:
- English baseline (top): `Unsaved changes` / `1 unsaved change` / `3 unsaved changes` / `12 unsaved changes` / `No changes`, plus `Form` / `Raw` / `Open` / `Clear` / `Save` / `Saving…` / `Apply` / `Applying…` / `Update` / `Updating…`, with `Search settings…` placeholder, `Quick Settings` accordion, and `Raw mode disabled…` notice.
- Simplified Chinese (middle): `未保存的更改` / `1 项未保存的更改` / `3 项未保存的更改` / `12 项未保存的更改` / `无更改`, plus `表单` / `原始` / `打开` / `清除` / `保存` / `保存中…` / `应用` / `应用中…` / `更新` / `正在更新…`, with `搜索设置…` placeholder, `快捷设置` accordion, and `原始模式已禁用…` notice.
- Traditional Chinese (bottom): `未儲存的變更` / `1 項未儲存的變更` / `3 項未儲存的變更` / `12 項未儲存的變更` / `無變更`, plus `表單` / `原始` / `開啟` / `清除` / `儲存` / `儲存中…` / `套用` / `套用中…` / `更新` / `正在更新…`, with `搜尋設定…` placeholder, `快速設定` accordion, and `原始模式已停用…` notice.

All badges and buttons fit comfortably; counts substitute correctly into the `{count}` placeholder; sing/plural correctly diverges in English (`change` vs `changes`) while staying identical in Chinese (Chinese doesn't pluralize); ellipses on `Applying…` / `Updating…` and Chinese equivalents render cleanly.

Live runtime read of the regenerated bundles, captured by dynamically importing the modules in the browser dev console against the running Vite dev server:

```
en.settings.unsavedChangeCount       -> "{count} unsaved change"
en.settings.unsavedChangesCount      -> "{count} unsaved changes"
zh_CN.settings.unsavedChangeCount    -> "{count} 项未保存的更改"
zh_CN.settings.unsavedChangesCount   -> "{count} 项未保存的更改"
zh_TW.settings.unsavedChangeCount    -> "{count} 項未儲存的變更"
zh_TW.settings.unsavedChangesCount   -> "{count} 項未儲存的變更"

en.common.save        -> "Save"
en.common.saving      -> "Saving…"
zh_CN.common.save     -> "保存"
zh_CN.common.saving   -> "保存中…"
zh_TW.common.save     -> "儲存"
zh_TW.common.saving   -> "儲存中…"
```

Real `pnpm ui:i18n:check` console output (post-patch, locally on the branch):

```
control-ui-i18n: raw-copy: baseline entries=646
zh-CN: clean (fallbacks=0)
zh-TW: clean (fallbacks=0)
pt-BR: clean (fallbacks=20)
de:    clean (fallbacks=20)
... 16 more locales reporting clean
```

`fallbacks=0` for zh-CN and zh-TW confirms the new keys (including `unsavedChangeCount` and `unsavedChangesCount`) are TM-backed translations, not English fallback. Supplemental signals: vitest 80/80 passed on the @clawsweeper acceptance set, oxlint reported 0 errors on touched files, tsgo:core exited 0.

Observed result after fix: `ui/src/ui/views/config.ts` has no remaining hardcoded chrome strings in the toolbar region, including the previously English-only form-mode count badge. `pnpm ui:i18n:check` no longer reports raw-copy baseline drift for the strings previously listed. `zh-CN` and `zh-TW` locale bundles render the Settings toolbar in native Chinese including the count badge variants and the Save/Saving button text, verified live in a real Chrome dev session against the running Vite dev server. TM entries seeded for both Chinese locales (all 22 new settings.* keys) so the translations persist across future maintainer sync runs.

What was not tested: Full end-to-end Settings interaction with a live OpenClaw gateway (visual verification was done in the live dev server; interaction-level behavior is covered by the vitest browser tests). Other 16 non-Chinese locales — translations fall through to English fallback because no translation provider was configured in this run, matching existing pipeline behavior for new keys. The deferred Phase 2 / Phase 3 scopes listed in the Out of scope section above were also not touched.

target.title: fix(parallel): resolve env search key refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes Parallel web search credential resolution when the configured API key is an env-backed SecretRef. The provider previously used the older strict config string reader, so SecretRef objects did not behave like direct `apiKey` strings or the documented `PARALLEL_API_KEY` fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

Parallel now uses the shared web-search credential resolver, matching the credential contract used by provider-local web search runtimes: direct configured values win, env SecretRefs resolve from their referenced env var, and the provider env fallback is used only when no credential is configured.

## User Impact

Users can configure `plugins.entries.parallel.config.webSearch.apiKey` as an env SecretRef without needing a live key in config. Missing or unsupported SecretRefs fail closed instead of silently falling back to an unrelated ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY` value.

## Evidence

- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts -- --reporter=verbose` passed, 1 file / 35 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts` passed.
- `OPENCLAW_HEAVY_CHECK_LOCK_SCOPE=worktree node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs extensions/parallel/src/parallel-web-search-provider.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine claude` reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- Default Codex autoreview was attempted first but the local OpenAI API key is rejected with 401, so it could not produce a review.

## Proof

- Added dispatch-level coverage through `createParallelWebSearchProvider().createTool(...).execute(...)`, lazy runtime loading, plugin-owned `plugins.entries.parallel.config.webSearch.apiKey`, scoped config merge, and the mocked trusted endpoint request.
- The resolved env SecretRef test proves the actual request header `x-api-key` is the configured env ref value and not the ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY` fallback.
- The unavailable env SecretRef test sets ambient `PARALLEL_API_KEY`, configures a missing env SecretRef, expects `missing_parallel_api_key`, and proves zero endpoint calls were made.
- Resolver-level coverage remains for direct configured keys, documented env fallback, default/custom env SecretRefs, and unavailable/unsupported SecretRefs.
- No `PARALLEL_API_KEY` is available in this environment. A local loopback HTTP proof attempt was intentionally blocked by OpenClaw's trusted web-search SSRF guard, so no fake local endpoint was used as live Parallel proof.

target.title: feat(skills): preview proposals before approval
target.body:
Closes #103871

## Summary

- add a read-only `review` action to `skill_workshop`
- render create proposals as their complete canonical applied skill and update proposals as unified diffs
- bound previews with line-aware pagination, proposal-version binding, and explicit drift/integrity outcomes
- keep presentation portable so channels can attach “View skill” / “View diff” actions without Skill Workshop policy

## What Problem This Solves

Approval messages currently provide only a prose summary. Operators cannot inspect the exact skill that a create proposal will install or see additions and removals in an update before approving it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The review projection belongs beside Skill Workshop validation and apply semantics, not in Telegram or another transport. The service computes the canonical read-only result; the agent tool owns bounded presentation and pagination.

## User Impact

Existing Proposal-ID-only lifecycle flows remain compatible. New review flows can bind later pages and apply/reject/quarantine decisions to `proposal_version`, preventing a reviewed proposal from silently changing before the decision. Approval requests resolved by skill name now carry the resolved proposal ID as well as its version into execution.

## Evidence

- 239 focused Vitest tests pass on the final rebased commit.
- Production and test tsgo checks pass.
- Exact-file oxlint/oxfmt, docs formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.
- Fresh structured autoreview found and prompted one approval-parameter fix; review of both that fix and the final 115,842-character branch bundle then reported no accepted/actionable findings.
- A live Telegram DM flow was operator-tested with create/update review, English labels, approval/rejection actions retained beside View, and lifecycle actions available from the first page of a paginated review.
- The broad remote `pnpm check:changed` lane could not start from this host: the configured Blacksmith client is absent and the AWS fallback broker is not authenticated. GitHub CI remains the broad remote gate.

## Verification

```bash
OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs \
  src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts \
  src/skills/workshop/policy.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/skill-workshop-tool.test.ts \
  src/agents/tool-mutation.test.ts \
  src/agents/system-prompt.test.ts \
  src/agents/agent-tools.before-tool-call.embedded-mode.test.ts

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental \
  --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo

node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.core.test.json --incremental \
  --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core-test.tsbuildinfo

node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs $(git diff --name-only upstream/main...HEAD -- '*.ts')
pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/skills/workshop/policy.ts src/skills/workshop/policy.test.ts
pnpm format:docs:check
git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD
.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main
```

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: preview the exact canonical result of a Skill Workshop proposal before approval and bind the later lifecycle decision to that reviewed version.
Real environment tested: live Telegram DM on the deployed production-patched OpenClaw runtime, operator-tested by the reporter.
Exact steps or command run after this patch: open a pending create/update proposal with View; inspect English-default labels; confirm Accept and Reject remain beside View; open a paginated review and verify Accept and Reject are present on page 1.
Evidence after fix: the operator confirmed View displayed the proposal content/diff, English labels rendered, all three actions remained together, and paginated page 1 exposed lifecycle actions.
Observed result after fix: creates and updates can be reviewed without losing direct approval/rejection, including before advancing a paginated review; stale decisions remain version-bound.
What was not tested: a separate Crabbox recording on the final rebased SHA; the configured Blacksmith client is unavailable on this host and the AWS fallback requires broker login.

## AI assistance

AI-assisted: yes. Codex implemented the change, ran focused validation, and completed repeated code-review passes. No agent transcript is attached.

target.title: fix(zai): add User-Agent header to endpoint detection probe
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: z.ai's endpoint auto-detection (`detectZaiEndpoint`) fails silently for Coding Plan API keys. The probe request sent by `probeZaiChatCompletions` in `extensions/zai/detect.ts` lacks a `User-Agent` header. z.ai's edge infrastructure rejects User-Agent-less requests with HTTP 429 (error code 1305: "The service may be temporarily overloaded"), causing all detection probes to fail and the function to return `null`. As a result, new users onboarding with z.ai Coding Plan keys cannot auto-detect the correct endpoint and must manually configure `baseUrl`, receiving misleading "rate limit" errors.

**Solution**: Add a `User-Agent` header to the `probeZaiChatCompletions` request, using the existing `openclaw/${version}` format already established in `src/agents/auth-profiles/usage.ts` and `src/infra/provider-usage.fetch.codex.ts`. The version is sourced from `process.env.OPENCLAW_VERSION` with a `"dev"` fallback when the environment variable is not set, matching the pattern established in `usage.ts`. The fix is purely additive — one header line in an existing request.

**What changed**: `extensions/zai/detect.ts` — added `const version = process.env.OPENCLAW_VERSION?.trim()` and `"user-agent": \`openclaw/${version || "dev"}\`` to the probe headers (2 lines). `extensions/zai/detect.test.ts` — added a new test that validates the `user-agent` header is present in probe requests (16 lines).

**What did NOT change**: No changes to the detection logic, timeout handling, or error handling. No changes to any other provider's endpoint detection. No changes to the real model transport path (which already sends User-Agent). No new dependencies, no API surface changes.

Fixes #98100

---

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**:
Users onboarding z.ai with a Coding Plan API key experience silent endpoint detection failure. `detectZaiEndpoint` returns `null`, the config falls back to the standard `https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4` endpoint, and the Coding Plan key (which is only authorized on the coding endpoint `https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4`) gets HTTP 429 on every real call. This produces misleading "rate limit" or "billing" error messages that obscure the real issue.

**Why This Change Was Made**:
The fix is minimal and targeted: adding one HTTP header to the existing probe request. Alternative approaches considered:
- Adding a default User-Agent globally to all `fetch` calls — rejected as too broad a change with potential side effects on other providers
- Using a format-specific User-Agent like `openclaw-zai-probe` — rejected in favor of consistency with the existing `openclaw/${version}` pattern
- Using a hardcoded version string — rejected because it would drift from the actual deployed version over time

The chosen approach is the simplest possible change that resolves the issue while maintaining consistency with the rest of the codebase.

**User Impact**:
- **Before**: z.ai Coding Plan users must manually run `openclaw config set models.providers.zai.baseUrl https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4` after onboarding
- **After**: onboarding auto-selects the correct Coding Plan endpoint, matching the behavior users expect
- No impact on existing users who already have their baseUrl configured
- No impact on users of non-Coding Plan z.ai keys (standard and CN endpoints)

---

## Root cause

**Trigger condition**:
Any z.ai onboarding flow with a Coding Plan API key. The `detectZaiEndpoint` function probes multiple endpoint candidates sequentially; without a User-Agent header, every probe (global, cn, coding-global, coding-cn) receives HTTP 429 from z.ai's edge.

**Root cause analysis**:
1. `probeZaiChatCompletions` (`extensions/zai/detect.ts:55-73`) sends a POST request to each candidate endpoint
2. The request headers at line 61-63 only include `authorization` and `content-type`
3. Node.js `fetch` (undici) does not add a default `User-Agent` header
4. z.ai's CDN/edge layer rejects User-Agent-less requests with HTTP 429 (code 1305)

target.title: fix(matrix): add mm: namespace prefix to THINKING_TAG_RE in monitor replies
target.body:
## Summary

**Problem**: The `THINKING_TAG_RE` and `THINKING_BLOCK_RE` regex patterns in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.ts` recognized bare thinking tags and `antml:` namespaced tags but not `mm:` namespaced MiniMax reasoning tags. When a MiniMax model produced reasoning output behind a Matrix channel, raw `<mm:think>` / `<mm:thought>` tags leaked through to end users instead of being suppressed.

**Solution**: Add `(?:antml:|mm:)?` prefix alternative to the `think(?:ing)?|thought` group in both regex constants. This matches the fix applied to 6 other channel/processing modules in prior PRs (#93767, #93806, #93820).

**What changed**: Two regex constants in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.ts` (lines 8-11). The alternatives group was restructured to add `mm:` namespace prefix support.

```typescript
// Before (missing mm: namespace):
/(?:think(?:ing)?|thought|antthinking)/

// After (all known namespace prefixes):
/(?:(?:antml:|mm:)?(?:think(?:ing)?|thought)|antthinking)/
```

**What did NOT change**: The `shouldSuppressReasoningReplyText()` function logic, `deliverMatrixReplies()` public API, message sending, media handling, thread/reply routing. All previously-matched tag patterns continue to work identically — the change is strictly additive.

Fixes #99412

## Linked context

- **Related PRs**: #93767 (core reasoning-tags), #93806 (silent-reply/streaming), #93820 (iMessage)
- **In scope**: Matrix monitor `replies.ts` regex constants
- **Out of scope**: End-to-end Matrix homeserver integration (requires live MiniMax API key)

## Root Cause

**Trigger condition**: MiniMax model (or Fireworks-provider inlining `mm:` prefixed reasoning) produces reasoning via Matrix channel. The `shouldSuppressReasoningReplyText()` regex lacked `mm:` namespace prefix, so reasoning tags passed through as visible text.

**Root cause**: Each channel module maintains its own local copy of thinking-tag regex patterns. When `mm:` support was added to the core `reasoning-tags.ts` (#93767), this matrix module was missed. This is the 4th and final instance of this synchronization gap.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: `mm:think` / `mm:thought` reasoning tags in Matrix channel messages are now detected and suppressed by `deliverMatrixReplies()`.
**Real environment tested**: Windows 10 LTSC 2019, Node.js v22.11.0, openclaw @ commit f007f75aab
**Exact steps or command run after this patch**: Added 3 regression tests in `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.test.ts` exercising the real `deliverMatrixReplies()` function: (1) pure `mm:` reasoning suppression, (2) mixed `mm:` reasoning + visible text delivery, (3) backward compatibility with `antml:` namespace. All tests pass against the actual function (not inline regex snippets).
**After-fix evidence**: All 9 tests pass including 3 new regression tests and 1 existing reasoning suppression test. Test output: `✓ suppresses reasoning-only text before Matrix sends`, `✓ suppresses mm: namespace reasoning tags before Matrix sends`, `✓ delivers mixed mm: reasoning and visible text as a single reply`, `✓ still suppresses antml: namespace reasoning (backward compatibility)`. Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 9 passed (9), Duration 1.88s.
**Observed result after the fix**: `deliverMatrixReplies()` correctly suppresses pure `mm:` reasoning replies, delivers mixed reasoning+visible replies, and maintains backward compatibility with all existing tag formats (bare, `antml:`, `antthinking`, `Reasoning:` prefix).
**What was not tested**: End-to-end Matrix homeserver integration with a live MiniMax model producing `mm:think` tags. This would require a running Matrix server + MiniMax API key. The fix has been verified through: (1) 3 dedicated regression tests exercising the real `deliverMatrixReplies()` function, (2) 6 other channel modules running the same regex pattern in production since #93767 with zero regressions, (3) the existing reasoning suppression test suite continuing to pass.

## Tests and validation

Regression tests added to `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.test.ts`:
```bash
npx vitest run extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.test.ts
```
Test Files 1 passed (1), Tests 9 passed (9), Duration 1.88s

The 3 new tests cover: (1) pure `mm:` reasoning suppression, (2) mixed `mm:` reasoning + visible text delivery, (3) backward compatibility with `antml:` namespace.

target.title: fix(agents): keep exact tool allowlists on owning factories
target.body:
Closes #104208

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users or jobs with exact embedded-run tool allowlists could lose the requested tool when its hand-maintained factory classification had drifted. `transcripts` was routed away from its core factory, while plugin-owned `canvas` was routed away from plugin construction.

## Why This Change Was Made

Core tool identity and factory family now live in one lightweight typed catalog. The attempt planner classifies each normalized allowlist once, while plugin, MCP, and LSP discovery remain on their existing runtime paths.

## User Impact

Exact allowlists now expose `transcripts` and `canvas` through their actual owners. Future core-tool additions have catalog-to-factory regression coverage instead of requiring parallel name maps to remain synchronized manually.

## Evidence

- Source-built ephemeral Gateway E2E at exact head `fe131d2951de20ff0e8488f4b8bc552e42996b16` under Node 24: two ordinary CLI-created one-shot isolated cron jobs completed with status `ok`; captured model requests advertised exactly `transcripts` for `toolsAllow: ["transcripts"]` and exactly `canvas` for `toolsAllow: ["canvas"]`. Only the model transport was mocked; Gateway, scheduler, embedded runner, planner, and core/plugin factories were real.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx7tfhjkkf9czp9y7b48mcjf`: 84/84 focused planner and core-factory tests passed.
- Same Testbox: 72/72 broader agent-tool construction tests passed.
- Same Testbox: `pnpm check:changed` passed, including production/test typechecks, changed-file lint, import-cycle and architecture guards.
- `autoreview --mode local --engine codex --thinking high`: clean; no accepted/actionable findings.
- Distill/Greybeard pass replaced repeated family scans and linear descriptor lookup with one normalized classification pass plus a process-stable map.
- Rebased onto current `main` without conflict; stable patch id remained `194567780968c1c7b85bba4f1dee3fb8ed7d2cb5`.
- Exact-head PR CI run `29142082269`: 44 jobs passed. The sole failure is unrelated `src/flows/doctor-health-contributions.test.ts` inventory drift; this PR touches only `src/agents/**`.

target.title: fix(signal): add timeouts to container REST requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal container REST requests already had a timeout around the fetch call, but the timer was cleared as soon as response headers arrived. A slow or hanging response body could still block REST send/status and attachment paths indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing timeout active until callers finish reading or releasing the response body. The change preserves the existing fetch helper, bounded body readers, cleanup path, and caller upload/attachment semantics.

## User Impact

If the signal-cli REST container returns headers and then stalls, OpenClaw now aborts the request during body reading instead of leaving Signal operations pending forever.

target.title: fix(discord): add timeouts to PluralKit lookup requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Discord PluralKit lookups are optional inbound message enrichment, but the PluralKit fetch and response body read did not have a deadline. A slow third-party API response could hold Discord message preflight open instead of degrading cleanly.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add a small PluralKit lookup timeout, preserve the caller abort signal from preflight, and keep the timer active until the API body has been read. Existing 404 handling, bounded error body reads, auth headers, and optional enrichment semantics are unchanged.

## User Impact

If PluralKit is slow or hangs, Discord inbound message handling can abort the lookup instead of waiting indefinitely, keeping the core message flow responsive.

target.title: test(extensions): derive Firecrawl batch expectations from tracked tests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `scripts/test-extension.mjs` tests hard-coded the Firecrawl extension as having exactly two tracked test files. That made the tooling test brittle: when Firecrawl gains or removes tests, the batch-plan assertions and exact-exclude coverage can go stale independently of the extension test planner's real inventory.

## Why This Change Was Made

Use the existing `listTrackedTestFilesForRoots()` helper to derive Firecrawl's tracked test files from the same inventory source as the extension test planner. The assertions now verify the planner output against the current tracked Firecrawl tests instead of a manually maintained pair of filenames.

## User Impact

No runtime behavior change. This only makes the extension test tooling coverage track Firecrawl's actual test inventory, so future Firecrawl test additions do not silently leave the batch exclude assertions under-covered.

## Evidence

Exact head: `12d74a8b5298d2b9b078d1c9615fc256e2298cfe`

target.title: fix(outbound): preserve backticks on <code> tags with attributes
target.body: Closes #104117 ## What Problem This Solves Fixes an issue where inline code blocks emitted by models with attributes—such as `foo()`—lost their backtick wrapping when OpenClaw converted outbound HTML to plain text for channels. The current sanitizer only matched a bare `` opener, so attributed tags fell through to the generic HTML stripper and arrived at the channel as raw text. ## Why This Change Was Made Updated the regex in `src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.ts` to accept optional attributes on the opening `` tag (`/]*)?>(.*?)<\/code>/gi`), matching the existing treatment of `]*>` and `]*>` in the same function. Added a focused unit test covering `class` and multiple attributes. ## User Impact Users on Telegram, iMessage, IRC, Google Chat, WhatsApp, and other channels that rely on `sanitizeForPlainText` will now see inline code rendered with backticks even when the model produces attributed `` tags, improving readability of code snippets in channel messages. ## Evidence ### Reproduced behavior on current `main` The bug is deterministic from the source: `/(.*?)<\/code>/gi` does not match ``, so the tag is stripped by the generic `HTML_TAG_RE` remover. ### After-fix runtime proof (public SDK export) The patched helper is the same `openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-outbound` export that Telegram, iMessage, and other channel adapters import at runtime: ```bash $ ./node_modules/.bin/tsx -e "import { sanitizeForPlainText } from 'openclaw/plugin-sdk/channel-outbound'; console.log('attributed:', sanitizeForPlainText('foo()')); console.log('plain:', sanitizeForPlainText('bar()'));" attributed: `foo()` plain: `bar()` ``` ### Unit tests ```bash $ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts ✓ |unit-fast| src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts (29 tests) 17ms ``` ### CI note Rebased onto `upstream/main` (`dfa31af0d4`) to resolve the `CHANGELOG.md does not contain a release section for 2026.7.2` failure in the QA Smoke CI build. That error was caused by the branch being behind `main` (still on `2026.6.11`) while the smoke packaging step expected the current release-train version; it is unrelated to this code change.

target.title: fix(agents): keep scp stderr tail UTF-16 safe
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where SCP stderr tail truncation can produce invalid Unicode when sandbox filenames contain emoji or other supplementary-plane characters.

`appendScpStderrTail()` caps raw `child.stderr` output with `combined.slice(-maxChars)` before the text is surfaced in `throw new Error(\`scp failed (${code}): ${stderr.trim()}\`)`. SCP stderr is unfiltered (unlike treemap label sanitization), so paths like `📊report.csv` can land on a UTF-16 surrogate boundary and leave a lone high surrogate in operator/agent-visible errors.

**Concrete example:** `appendScpStderrTail("prefix", "🤖tail", 5)` with the old slice could keep `U+D83D` without its low half; the thrown error then carries malformed Unicode.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replace the raw tail slice with `sliceUtf16Safe(combined, Math.max(0, combined.length - maxChars))` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`, matching the established tail-truncation pattern in `src/infra/restart-sentinel.ts` (#103757) and `src/node-host/invoke.ts`. Ring-buffer size and SCP behavior are unchanged; only the truncation boundary is surrogate-safe.

## User Impact

**Before:** SCP failures for media staging can surface replacement glyphs or invalid Unicode in agent/operator error text when stderr mentions emoji filenames near the tail cap.

**After:** SCP stderr tails remain well-formed Unicode; boundary emoji are dropped whole instead of split.

## Evidence

- `src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.ts` — `appendScpStderrTail` uses `sliceUtf16Safe` for the tail cap
- `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.ts` — shared surrogate backoff helper
- Helper regression: `src/auto-reply/reply.stage-sandbox-media.scp-remote-path.test.ts`
- Caller-path regression: `src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.scp.test.ts` (`testing.scpFile` mocked `spawn` stderr bisect case)
- Live subprocess proof: production `testing.scpFile` and `stageSandboxMedia` exercised with the real `/usr/bin/scp` binary (no `spawn` mock)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** SCP stderr tail truncation no longer leaves unpaired UTF-16 surrogates when an emoji filename crosses the tail cap before the error is thrown to the agent/operator.
- **Canonical reachability path:** `stageSandboxMedia` remote attachment staging → `scpFile` spawns `scp` → `child.stderr` chunks → `appendScpStderrTail` ring buffer → `finish(new Error(\`scp failed (${code}): ${stderr.trim()}\`))` on non-zero exit.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; real OpenSSH `scp` subprocess via production `testing.scpFile`, plus `stageSandboxMedia` remote-cache path with emoji attachment filename and captured runtime log line.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused `sliceUtf16Safe` from `@openclaw/normalization-core/utf16-slice`; provider/channel constraints N/A because this is sandbox media staging stderr handling.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS (darwin 24.3.0), Node 22, branch `fix/scp-stderr-tail-utf16` @ `e8222a145cc`, real `/usr/bin/scp` against `git@github.com` (public host; no operator credentials printed).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
$ pnpm install   # once, in repo root with devDependencies
$ pnpm exec tsx -e "
import fs from 'node:fs/promises';
import os from 'node:os';
import path from 'node:path';
import { testing } from './src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.ts';
(async () => {
  const tmp = await fs.mkdtemp(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'scp-live-proof-'));
  try {
    await testing.scpFile('git@github.com', '/tmp/🤖missing.jpg', path.join(tmp, 'download'));
  } catch (error) {
    console.log(error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error));
  } finally {
    await fs.rm(tmp, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
})();
"

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply.stage-sandbox-media.scp-remote-path.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/stage-sandbox-media.scp.test.ts -t "UTF-16|scp stderr tail|scpFile" --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node --import tsx …testing.scpFile('git@github.com', '/tmp/🤖missing.jpg', …)
scp failed (255): subsystem request failed on channel 0
scp: Connection closed

$ OPENCLAW_LIVE_TEST=1 node --import tsx -e "
…stageSandboxMedia({ remoteMediaMode: 'cache', ctx.MediaRemoteHost: 'git@github.com', MediaPath: '/Users/demo/Library/Messages/Attachments/ab/cd/📊report.jpg', … })
"
Failed to stage inbound media path /Users/demo/Library/Messages/Attachments/ab/cd/📊report.jpg: Error: scp failed (255): subsystem request failed on channel 0
scp: Connection closed
unpaired_surrogates=false

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs … -t "UTF-16|scp stderr tail|scpFile" --reporter=verbose
 ✓ keeps scp stderr tail UTF-16 safe when the boundary bisects an emoji
 ✓ surfaces UTF-16 safe scp stderr when transfer fails with emoji at tail boundary

Test Files  2 passed (2)
     Tests  5 passed | 5 skipped (10)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Live production `scpFile` retained real `scp` stderr through `appendScpStderrTail` and surfaced a well-formed `scp failed (255): …` message with `unpaired_surrogates=false`. `stageSandboxMedia` reached the same production path for an emoji remote attachment filename and logged a well-formed failure without splitting surrogate pairs. Supplemental mocked caller regression still proves the 16,384-code-unit emoji low-surrogate tail boundary that natural short `scp` stderr does not reach in this environment.
- **What was not tested:** Live `scp` against a reachable operator sandbox host with >16,384 code units of stderr before the emoji filename error; full gateway/iMessage inbound delivery roundtrip.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor)
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns
- Single commit on `upstream/main`; no bundled `scripts/` or release-script changes

target.title: fix(session): stop repeated restart recovery after retry budget
target.body:
Related: #95750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a gateway restart loop where the same interrupted main session can be accepted for automatic recovery on every boot. Supervisor backoff does not make the session healthy, so attempts separated by minutes or hours must still consume one durable recovery budget.

## Why This Change Was Made

Main-session restart recovery now has one canonical persisted fuse: `SessionEntry.mainRestartRecovery`.

- `automaticAttempts` counts accepted or acceptance-uncertain automatic recoveries since the last non-aborted run settlement on the same session.
- The first three recoveries may dispatch. An exhausted row is tombstoned before a fourth dispatch, with no elapsed-time expiry.
- A recovery attempt is reserved under the session-store writer lock before Gateway dispatch. The reservation is rolled back only when the request is known not to have been accepted; post-dispatch transport uncertainty keeps the attempt charged.
- Gateway admission revalidates the exact session and reservation identity before accepting a recovery run.
- Foreground admissions use a lifecycle-generation-scoped token set to fence concurrent recovery scans. Each admission releases only its own token on unaccepted, undispatched, or settled paths, so overlapping foreground requests cannot expose or permanently suppress recovery.
- A run that reaches normal session-store settlement without `aborted` clears `mainRestartRecovery`, including background progress that does not touch interaction/activity metadata. Session replacement and reset also clear it.
- `restartRecoveryRuns` remains lifecycle suppression only; it is not used to derive the durable retry budget.
- Subagent orphan recovery retains its separate policy: two attempts in the existing two-minute rapid re-wedge window.
- Tombstone state is committed before the best-effort operator notice is sent, so a stale or failed notification cannot race the quarantine decision.
- Doctor reports wedged main and subagent sessions and can clear only stale `abortedLastRun` flags that conflict with an existing tombstone; it does not re-enable automatic recovery.
- Session-store cache identity uses nanosecond `ctime`/`mtime` plus size so same-size writes inside one millisecond cannot hide recovery or Doctor updates.

This adds no public config, environment variable, wire protocol, provider route, or plugin API.

## User Impact

A wedged main session can no longer trigger unbounded automatic resume across Gateway restarts. After three accepted or acceptance-uncertain recovery attempts, OpenClaw quarantines the session before another automatic dispatch and asks the operator to inspect it and use `/new` or reset.

Healthy progress restores the full budget. The fuse does not expire merely because time passes.

## Evidence

Current branch:

```text
base: upstream/main@99ddde87262
head: 2408915c9ce
```

Current-head local static proof:

```text
node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --write src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs src/gateway/server-methods/agent.ts src/gateway/server-methods/agent.test.ts
git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD
.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main
```

The final autoreview reported no accepted/actionable findings. Local runtime tests were intentionally not run because this is contributor/fork code and the repository requires secretless fork CI or sanitized AWS Crabbox; the available sanitized AWS environment had no IMDS role.

Exact-head CI for `2408915c9ce`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29142465164

- Passed the Gateway test shard, build, lint, production types, test types, guards, dependency checks, and the other PR-relevant jobs.
- The run has two inherited failures that reproduce unchanged on the already-merged #104210: stale `docs/docs_map.md` output for `Resident local STT`, and the missing `core/doctor/local-audio-acceleration` contribution in `doctor-health-contributions.test.ts`. They are outside this PR's diff and were not folded into this branch.

Focused regression coverage in the branch includes:

- cumulative attempts across slow restart intervals and tombstone-before-fourth behavior;
- pre-dispatch rollback versus post-dispatch acceptance uncertainty;
- exact reservation identity and stale scan rejection;
- concurrent foreground owner tokens, per-owner release, and settlement cleanup;
- successful/background progress reset and session reset/replacement cleanup;
- Doctor reporting/repair and main/subagent ownership separation;
- session-store cache invalidation for same-size rapid rewrites.

Prior real Telegram Desktop behavior proof remains applicable to the user-visible recovery path:

- Workflow: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28780448010
- Artifact bundle: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/28780448010/artifacts/8106022765
- Manifest: https://artifacts.openclaw.ai/mantis/telegram-desktop/pr-96230/run-28780448010-1/index.json

The baseline replayed the exhausted recovery turn before handling a fresh message. The candidate quarantined the exhausted row and handled the fresh Telegram message without another automatic resume.

target.title: fix(codex): preserve UTF-16 pairs in tool output delta truncation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Codex streaming tool output display renders a corrupted glyph ("�") when a non-BMP character (emoji like 😀) straddles the 8,000-character progress-message truncation boundary. The raw `.slice(0, remainingChars)` on the emitted delta cuts at a UTF-16 code-unit boundary — when `remainingChars` lands on the HIGH surrogate of a surrogate pair, the truncated progress message carries a dangling `\uD83D` that corrupts the rendered output in the chat transcript.

## Why This Change Was Made

`truncateUtf16Safe` is already imported on line 29 and used at two other call sites in the same file (lines 3413, 3435) for the 10,000-char transcript-output path. This single progress-message call site at line 1447 was missed during the original import. The fix reuses the canonical helper — no new abstraction, no new import.

## User Impact

Streaming tool output in the Codex chat UI no longer renders a corrupted replacement character when model-generated tool output contains emoji characters near the 8,000-character progress limit. ASCII-only output is unaffected.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** A non-BMP character (emoji surrogate pair) that straddles the `TOOL_PROGRESS_OUTPUT_MAX_CHARS` (8,000) boundary in the Codex event projector's `handleOutputDelta` progress-message path must not produce a lone surrogate in the emitted transcript text.

**Real environment tested:** Node.js v22.22.0, x64, linux, OpenClaw checkout at `2d0d06d3f1`

### Evidence after fix — standalone runtime proof

A standalone Node.js script (`proof-codex-projector-runtime.mts`) imports the real `CodexAppServerEventProjector` class directly from `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.ts`, drives it through `handleNotification` with `verboseLevel: "full"`, and prints the actual `onToolResult` callback text. This is NOT a test framework — it is a real process executing the production code path.

```
── [Case 1] remainingChars=1, delta=😀hello ──
onToolResult calls: 3
[call 0] len=32 lone=false
🛠️ `show emoji.txt (workspace)`
---
[call 1] len=8019 lone=false
🛠️ Bash
```txt
aaaa...aaaa
```
---
[call 2] len=37 lone=false
🛠️ Bash
```txt
...(truncated)...
```
---
── [Case 2] remainingChars=2, delta=x😀y ──
onToolResult calls: 3
[call 0] len=33 lone=false
🛠️ `show emoji2.txt (workspace)`
---
[call 1] len=8018 lone=false
🛠️ Bash
```txt
aaaa...aaaa
```
---
[call 2] len=39 lone=false
🛠️ Bash
```txt
x
...(truncated)...
```
---

=== RUNTIME PROOF COMPLETE ===
node=v22.22.0
No lone surrogates in any emitted progress text.
Fix confirmed: truncateUtf16Safe in production projector.
```

**Case 1** — remainingChars=1, delta starts with 😀: `truncateUtf16Safe` detects the HIGH surrogate at position 0 and backs off, producing an empty chunk. The progress message is `...(truncated)...` — clean, no surrogate bytes.

**Case 2** — remainingChars=2, delta="x😀y": `truncateUtf16Safe` cuts at position 1 (the 'x'), backs off before the emoji at positions 1-2. The progress message is `x\n...(truncated)...` — clean, no surrogate bytes.

### Negative control (pre-fix behavior reproduced)

Same standalone script, same environment. `event-projector.ts` reverted to `origin/main` (`.slice(0, remainingChars)`) — the script picks up the old code via tsx on-the-fly compilation:

```
── [Case 1] remainingChars=1, delta=😀hello ──
[call 2] len=39 lone=true              ← BUG: lone surrogate detected!
🛠️ Bash
```txt
�                                     ← U+D83D HIGH surrogate, corrupted glyph
...(truncated)...
```
---
── [Case 2] remainingChars=2, delta=x😀y ──
[call 2] len=40 lone=true              ← BUG: lone surrogate detected!
🛠️ Bash
```txt
x�                                    ← "x" + U+D83D HIGH surrogate
...(truncated)...
```
---
```

**Case 1 old code:** `.slice(0, 1)` on `"😀hello"` cuts after the HIGH surrogate at position 0, producing `"\uD83D"` → the markdown-fenced progress message renders `�` (corrupted glyph).

**Case 2 old code:** `.slice(0, 2)` on `"x😀y"` cuts after the HIGH surrogate at position 1, producing `"x\uD83D"` → the progress message renders `x�`.

Restoring the fix — same script, same process — all calls show `lone=false`, clean text.

### Quantitative summary

| Metric | Old `.slice()` | Fix `truncateUtf16Safe` |
|--------|---------------|------------------------|
| Case 1 lone surrogates | 1 (`U+D83D`) | 0 |
| Case 2 lone surrogates | 1 (`U+D83D`) | 0 |
| Case 1 emitted chars at cap | 8,000 (includes split surrogate) | 7,999 (backed off) |
| Case 2 emitted chars at cap | 8,000 (includes split surrogate) | 7,999 (backed off) |

### What was not tested

- **Real Codex app-server process:** The projector is driven through its public `handleNotification` API with manually constructed events, not a live Codex Rust binary. The event shapes match the upstream Codex protocol (`item/commandExecution/outputDelta`), but a live session with model-generated emoji output at the exact 8,000-char boundary was not reproduced.
- **macOS / Windows:** Proof was collected on Linux x64 only. The fix is platform-independent (pure string manipulation in `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.ts`).
- **Non-bash tools:** Only `commandExecution` (tool name `"bash"`) was tested. Other tool types (`fileChange`, `mcpToolCall`) share the same `handleOutputDelta` entry point and the same `truncateUtf16Safe` call.

## Evidence

**Change surface:** 1 file, 1 line — `delta.slice(0, remainingChars)` → `truncateUtf16Safe(delta, remainingChars)` at `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.ts:1447`.

| Area | Files | Added | Removed | Net |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Source | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0 |
| Tests | 1 | 122 | 0 | +122 |
| **Total** | **2** | **123** | **1** | **+122** |

Test-to-fix ratio: 122:1 test lines per production line changed.

**Runtime proof:** `proof-codex-projector-runtime.mts` — standalone Node.js script (NOT a test framework) that imports the real `CodexAppServerEventProjector` class, drives it with `verboseLevel: "full"` and `onToolResult` callback, and prints the actual emitted text. Full positive and negative control output above in Real behavior proof.

**Vitest regression:** `extensions/codex/src/app-server/event-projector.test.ts` — new test "keeps streamed progress output UTF-16 safe at the 8,000-char progress message cap" (122 lines) covers 3 UTF-16 edge cases at the 8,000-char boundary. Adjacent UTF-16 tests pass (no regression on the 10,000-char transcript path).

**Canonical helper contract:** `truncateUtf16Safe` in `packages/normalization-core/src/utf16-slice.ts:44` retains the existing maximum-code-unit semantics but backs off when the truncation boundary falls between a valid HIGH and LOW surrogate. Already used at lines 3413 and 3435 in the same file.

**No competing PRs:** `gh search prs --repo openclaw/openclaw --state open "event-projector AND (utf16 OR surrogate OR truncateUtf16Safe)"` returns no open PRs covering the same call site.
