target.title: fix(feishu): drive info finds files past the first page
target.body:
Closes #93928

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Feishu users running `feishu_drive info` received `File not found` for files that were not present on the first page of the root drive listing.

## Why This Change Was Made

Drive info now queries Feishu's metadata API directly by file token and type instead of searching a single root-list response. Shortcut lookups retain the existing root-list behavior because the metadata endpoint does not support the shortcut type, and installations without the metadata scope fall back to the legacy lookup for compatibility.

## User Impact

Users can retrieve metadata for supported files regardless of the containing shared folder or root-list page. Existing read-only installations continue to support root-level info lookups, while direct lookups require `drive:drive.metadata:readonly` or the full `drive:drive` scope.

## Evidence

- `pnpm test extensions/feishu/src/drive.test.ts` — 24 tests passed
- `pnpm test:extension feishu` — 79 files and 1,123 tests passed
- Focused oxfmt and oxlint checks passed
- Documentation formatting and `git diff --check` passed
- Final Codex review reported no findings

### Redacted live Feishu proof

Validated on July 11, 2026 with an enabled enterprise app using application-identity `drive:drive.metadata:readonly`. No App Secret, tenant token, file token, title, owner ID, or URL is included below.

For an existing wiki document, Feishu resolved the wiki token to its underlying document metadata:

```json
{"httpStatus":200,"code":0,"metasCount":1,"returnedType":"docx","tokenLength":27,"hasTitle":true,"hasUrl":true,"requestType":"wiki","requestTokenMatches":true}
```

The PR's exact direct lookup shape was then used with that underlying `docx` token:

```json
{"httpStatus":200,"code":0,"metasCount":1,"tokenMatched":true,"returnedType":"docx","hasTitle":true,"hasUrl":true,"hasOwner":true,"hasCreateTime":true,"hasModifyTime":true}
```

The same app does not have the legacy root-list scope, so the old root request returned HTTP 400 / Feishu code `99991672`, while the direct metadata request above succeeded. This confirms direct info lookup works independently with the documented metadata-only scope.

An invalid `docx` token returned HTTP 200 with top-level `code: 0`, an empty `metas` array, and this per-document failure:

```json
{"failed_list":[{"code":970005,"token":"<redacted-invalid-token>"}]}
```

The missing-file regression test now mirrors that observed `failed_list` shape and confirms the tool reports `File not found`. Shortcut behavior and the legacy read-only fallback remain covered by focused mocked SDK tests; no existing app with exactly `drive:drive:readonly` and without metadata scope was available for a live fallback test.

After rebasing onto current `main`, production/test type checks are blocked by pre-existing errors in `extensions/feishu/src/presentation-card.ts` (`renderMessagePresentationTableFallbackText` missing and an unrelated `select`/`table` comparison). This PR does not modify that file.

target.title: fix(line): AI-assisted - requireMention can now optionally gate non-text messages with bounded pending-media retention
target.body:
Closes #103758

<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where LINE groups configured with `requireMention: true` could not require a mention before non-text messages (image/video/audio/file) reached the agent. Any photo, video, voice clip, or file posted in such a group was always processed, regardless of whether the bot was actually mentioned, because LINE's Messaging API never attaches mention metadata to non-text messages and the mention-gate logic could not account for that.

Fixes an issue where operators of mention-gated LINE groups would see the bot react to every image/video/audio/file dropped in the chat, even when nobody addressed the bot, when they expected the same "must be mentioned" behavior that already applies to text messages (per #34438 / #35847).

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds two new **opt-in** LINE group config fields — `requireMentionForNonText` and `pendingMediaLimit` — so operators can explicitly turn on mention gating for non-text messages without changing default behavior for anyone else. Because LINE never reports a mention on the non-text message itself, a bounded per-group pending-media queue (default limit 3) retains the most recent skipped media until a later message in the same group is mentioned and fully processed, at which point the queued media is attached to that turn and the queue is cleared. This lets a user post a photo, then follow up with `@bot look at this`, and have the photo still reach the agent.

A prior attempt at the opt-in flag alone (#68197) went stale without merging and did not include the retention queue, which meant skipped media was simply dropped forever once a group opted in — this PR keeps the same opt-in, default-false posture that maintainers asked for on #68197, and adds the missing retention piece on top.

## User Impact

LINE operators can now set `channels.line.accounts.<id>.groups.<groupId>.requireMentionForNonText: true` (alongside `requireMention: true`) to require an `@mention` before non-text messages reach the agent, matching the existing text-message behavior. Skipped media isn't lost — up to `pendingMediaLimit` (default 3) recent items are retained per group and delivered alongside the next mentioned message. Existing configs are unaffected since both fields default to off/unset.

## Evidence

`pnpm test:extension line` — 26 test files, **313 tests passing** (up from 307 on `main`; +6 in `bot-handlers.test.ts`, +2 in `config-schema.test.ts`):

```
 Test Files  26 passed (26)
      Tests  313 passed (313)
```

New tests cover:

- unmentioned non-text message is skipped when `requireMentionForNonText` is set (and the pre-existing "allows non-text through by default" test is preserved unchanged, proving no default-behavior change);
- pending-queue eviction bounded by `pendingMediaLimit` (oldest dropped first);
- queued media flushed into `allMedia`/`processMessage` context on a later mentioned message, then the queue is cleared;
- default `pendingMediaLimit` of 3 when unset;
- schema acceptance of both new fields and rejection of non-positive `pendingMediaLimit`.

Additional local validation:

- `npx tsc -p extensions/line/tsconfig.json --noEmit` — clean, exit 0
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/line` — 0 warnings/errors
- `node --import tsx scripts/generate-config-doc-baseline.ts --check` — passes after regenerating `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` for the new config surface
- `node scripts/format-docs.mjs --check` / `markdownlint-cli2` / `node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs` — all clean on `docs/channels/line.md`
- `codex` CLI was not available in this environment, so `codex review --base origin/main` could not be run locally; noting this per CONTRIBUTING.md instead of skipping silently.

---

### AI-assisted PR

target.title: fix(extensions/anthropic): preserve migrated model entries when inherited keys shadow converted refs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where adopting Claude CLI auth could silently drop a model's custom settings (aliases, parameters, etc.) or throw when the global `Object.prototype` contains an inherited property matching the converted Anthropic model ref.

## Why This Change Was Made

`rewriteModelEntryMap` used `converted in next` to decide whether to copy a legacy `claude-cli/*` entry to its Anthropic equivalent, and then assigned with `next[converted] = value`. The `in` operator follows the prototype chain, and the assignment can throw or invoke an inherited setter when `Object.prototype` is polluted. The migration could therefore skip the copy, delete the original `claude-cli/*` key, and lose the user's model configuration.

The change now:
- checks own-property membership with `Object.hasOwn`;
- writes migrated and seeded entries with `Object.defineProperty` so they become own properties even when `Object.prototype` has a getter-only accessor, non-writable data descriptor, or setter.

This applies the same own-entry invariant that #103373 adds to the Anthropic API-key default-allowlist seeding path.

## User Impact

Users whose runtime has a polluted `Object.prototype` no longer lose per-model aliases or other metadata, and no longer see migration throws, when adopting Claude CLI-backed Anthropic refs.

## Evidence

### Unit tests

```bash
pnpm test extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.test.ts --run
```

Result: 19 passed.

The regression suite covers four Object.prototype descriptor collisions and fails against the parent commit:
- inherited writable data descriptor;
- inherited non-writable data descriptor (throws before the fix);
- inherited getter-only accessor (throws before the fix);
- inherited setter accessor (entry becomes undefined before the fix, setter is not invoked after).

### Type / lint

```bash
pnpm tsgo:extensions        # exit 0
node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.extensions.json extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.test.ts extensions/anthropic/cli-migration.ts
```

Both pass.

### Live migration proof

Controlled run with an `Object.prototype` getter-only accessor shadowing the converted ref:

```text
=== Claude CLI auth adoption migration proof ===
Scenario: Object.prototype has a getter-only accessor for the converted ref.
Migrated entry: {
  "alias": "Work Opus",
  "temperature": 0.7,
  "agentRuntime": { "id": "claude-cli" }
}
Entry is own property: true
Alias preserved: true
Parameters preserved: true
```

The alias and `temperature` parameter survive migration, and the resulting entry is an own property of `models` rather than the inherited accessor value.

## Release Note

- Anthropic: preserve migrated model aliases and parameters when inherited prototype keys shadow converted Claude CLI refs.

Related: #103373

target.title: fix(agent-tools): add request timeout to remote media fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The agent-side image, image-generation, and PDF tools fetch remote media through `loadWebMedia` / `loadWebMediaRaw` with only a body-idle gap guard (`readIdleTimeoutMs`). A remote endpoint that accepts the TCP connection but withholds response headers forever leaves the fetch open indefinitely — `readIdleTimeoutMs` only governs gaps between body chunks, never the pre-header stall. This PR threads a 15-minute header-arrival deadline through the three agent-tool call sites so a never-responding endpoint fails fast while slow-but-progressing transfers keep going.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initial proposal exposed a new `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs?: number` (overall-request lifetime). ClawSweeper correctly rejected that as compatibility-breaking: it would have capped healthy bodies that keep yielding past 15 minutes. The narrower `FetchMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs` seam landed on `origin/main` via PR #103020 (merge commit `26aef8c48bc40d2ea456c2cfc3eca126dca33888`, 2026-07-10 13:31 UTC, currently reachable from `origin/main@bb26753705`) specifically for this stall class — header-only deadline via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`, `cleanup()`-ed once headers arrive so the body is not capped. This PR drops the parallel total-timeout surface and adopts that canonical seam end-to-end through the three agent-tool call sites.

## What Changed

- `src/media/web-media.ts` — `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs?: number` removed; replaced with `WebMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs?: number`. `loadWebMediaInternal` destructures the new field and forwards it conditionally into `readRemoteMediaBuffer({ ..., responseHeaderTimeoutMs })` so an unset value does not overwrite main's "no header deadline" default.
- `src/agents/tools/media-tool-shared.ts` — new export `REMOTE_MEDIA_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000` next to the existing `REMOTE_MEDIA_READ_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000`.
- `src/agents/tools/image-tool.ts:1042`, `image-generate-tool.ts:675`, `pdf-tool.ts:487` — on the `isHttpUrl` branch, the spread becomes `{ readIdleTimeoutMs: REMOTE_MEDIA_READ_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, responseHeaderTimeoutMs: REMOTE_MEDIA_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS }`.
- `src/agents/tools/{image,image-generate,pdf}-tool.test.ts` — the prior `timeoutMs: 15 * 60_000` assertions added by the previous version of this branch are removed (the canonical seam is now exercised end-to-end via the `loadWebMedia` forwarding layer; per-tool assertions would be redundant).
- `proof-103209-image-tool-layer.mts` — new live-run proof that exercises the canonical seam end-to-end through `loadWebMedia` (the entrypoint image-tool/image-generate-tool/pdf-tool invoke), real stalled HTTP server, real AbortSignal, surfaced error shape.

## User Impact

- Hard 15-minute upper bound on header-arrival latency for image, image-generation, and PDF tool calls against stalled remote endpoints.
- Healthy upstreams see no behavior change. **Slow-but-progressing transfers are explicitly NOT capped** — once headers arrive, the header deadline is cleared and `readIdleTimeoutMs` (120s for agent-tools) continues to bound chunk gaps.
- Users on very slow networks where headers legitimately take >15 min will see new failures. This matches the existing 15-minute ceiling from canonical precedent #103266 (`src/cli/nodes-camera.ts:20`, `CAMERA_URL_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS`); the trade-off has already been accepted by maintainers on that merge.

## Evidence

### Live behavior proof (image-tool entrypoint `loadWebMedia`, real HTTP server, real fetch, real AbortSignal, surfaced error shape)

Local fallback run (Crabbox unavailable in this env):

```
$ node node_modules/.bin/tsx proof-103209-image-tool-layer.mts
[proof] stalled HTTP server listening on http://127.0.0.1:35937
[proof] calling loadWebMedia (the entrypoint image-tool/image-generate-tool/pdf-tool invoke)
[proof] with responseHeaderTimeoutMs=1000ms (production uses 15*60_000)
```

target.title: fix(web-media): add timeoutMs option to WebMediaOptions for remote fetches
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`loadWebMedia` / `readRemoteMediaBuffer` had no upper bound on header-arrival latency. An unresponsive upstream could pin a Tlon media download or URL-backed image upload at the TCP/streaming-read layer until `readIdleTimeoutMs` finally tripped — and only if a body ever started. This PR threads a 15-minute header-arrival deadline through `WebMediaOptions` and the two Tlon call sites so a never-responding endpoint fails fast while slow-but-progressing transfers keep going.

## Why This Change Was Made

The initial proposal exposed a new `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs?: number` (overall-request lifetime). ClawSweeper correctly rejected that as compatibility-breaking: it would have capped healthy bodies that keep yielding past 15 minutes. The narrower `FetchMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs` seam landed on `origin/main` via PR #103020 (merge commit `26aef8c48bc40d2ea456c2cfc3eca126dca33888`, 2026-07-10 13:31 UTC, currently reachable from `origin/main@bb26753705`) specifically for this stall class — header-only deadline via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`, `cleanup()`-ed once headers arrive so the body is not capped. This PR drops the parallel total-timeout surface and adopts that canonical seam end-to-end.

## What Changed

- `src/media/web-media.ts` — `WebMediaOptions.timeoutMs?: number` removed; replaced with `WebMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs?: number`. `loadWebMediaInternal` destructures the new field and forwards it conditionally into `readRemoteMediaBuffer({ ..., responseHeaderTimeoutMs })` so an unset value does not overwrite main's "no header deadline" default.
- `src/media/web-media.test.ts` — replaces the prior "aborts a … via the overall timeoutMs deadline" test with **"forwards responseHeaderTimeoutMs from loadWebMediaRaw through readRemoteMediaBuffer"** (using `vi.useFakeTimers()` + a progressing body stream, identical to main's `fetch.test.ts:438-485` "clears the response-header deadline while a healthy body keeps progressing" pattern). Asserts the resolved buffer contains the enqueued bytes after the header deadline clears — proving the public seam actually forwards the field.
- `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/media.ts` — replaces `TLON_MEDIA_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS` with `TLON_MEDIA_DOWNLOAD_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000`; `downloadMedia`'s `fetchOptions` now forwards `responseHeaderTimeoutMs:` to both `saveRemoteMedia` and `readRemoteMediaBuffer`.
- `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.ts` — replaces `TLON_UPLOAD_IMAGE_TIMEOUT_MS` with `TLON_UPLOAD_IMAGE_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS = 15 * 60_000`; `uploadImageFromUrl`'s `readRemoteMediaBuffer` call forwards the same.
- `extensions/tlon/src/monitor/media.test.ts`, `extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.test.ts` — assertion relaxed to `expect.objectContaining({ ..., responseHeaderTimeoutMs: 15 * 60_000 })`.
- `proof-103206-tool-run.mts` — new live-run proof that exercises the canonical seam end-to-end (real stalled HTTP server + real `loadWebMedia` + real AbortSignal + surfaced error shape).

## User Impact

- Hard 15-minute upper bound on header-arrival latency for Tlon media downloads and URL-backed image uploads triggered by `extensions/tlon`.
- Healthy upstreams see no behavior change. **Slow-but-progressing transfers are explicitly NOT capped** — once headers arrive, the header deadline is cleared and `readIdleTimeoutMs` (30s for Tlon) continues to bound chunk gaps. This is the deliberate behavior change vs. the prior total-timeout proposal.
- Tlon users on very slow networks where headers legitimately take >15 min will see new failures. This matches the existing 15-minute ceiling from canonical precedent #103266 (`src/cli/nodes-camera.ts:20`, `CAMERA_URL_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS`); the trade-off has already been accepted by maintainers on that merge.

## Evidence

### Live behavior proof (real HTTP server, real fetch, real AbortSignal, surfaced error shape)

Local fallback run (Crabbox unavailable in this env):

```
$ node node_modules/.bin/tsx proof-103206-tool-run.mts
[proof] stalled HTTP server listening on http://127.0.0.1:36539
[proof] calling loadWebMedia with responseHeaderTimeoutMs=1000ms (production code path uses 15*60_000)
[proof] this exercises the canonical seam from PR #103020:
[proof]   loadWebMedia -> readRemoteMediaBuffer -> fetchGuardedMediaResponse
[proof]   -> fetchWithSsrFGuard -> buildTimeoutAbortSignal (response header deadline)
[proof]   -> globalThis.fetch
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 1000ms (elapsed 1001ms) operation=media response headers url=http://127.0.0.1:36539/never-responds.png
[proof] elapsed: 1154ms
[proof] surfaced error.name: MediaFetchError
[proof] surfaced error.code: fetch_failed
[proof] surfaced error.message: Failed to fetch media from http://127.0.0.1:36539/never-responds.png: request timed out
[proof] surfaced error.cause.name: TimeoutError
[proof] surfaced error.cause.message: request timed out
[proof] result: responseHeaderTimeoutMs fired through real production path
{
  "url": "http://127.0.0.1:36539/never-responds.png",
  "responseHeaderTimeoutMs": 1000,
  "outcome": {
    "kind": "error",
    "name": "MediaFetchError",
    "code": "fetch_failed",
    "message": "Failed to fetch media from http://127.0.0.1:36539/never-responds.png: request timed out",
    "causeName": "TimeoutError",
    "causeMessage": "request timed out",
    "elapsedMs": 1154
  },
  "passed": true
}
```

Key observations:
- **1154ms elapsed** (vs 1000ms `responseHeaderTimeoutMs`): the `[fetch-timeout]` log fires at the deadline, proving the AbortSignal fires at the configured header deadline.
- **Surfaced error shape**: `MediaFetchError { code: "fetch_failed", cause: TimeoutError("request timed out") }` — the exact error shape that propagates to the Tlon extension caller.

### Repository test (forwards responseHeaderTimeoutMs through the public seam)

Added in `src/media/web-media.test.ts > loadWebMedia > forwards responseHeaderTimeoutMs from loadWebMediaRaw through readRemoteMediaBuffer`. The test uses `vi.useFakeTimers()` and an `enqueue([1],25) → enqueue([2],50) → close(75)` body stream (matching main's pattern at `fetch.test.ts:438-485`). Asserts the resolved buffer equals the concatenation of enqueued bytes — proving the header deadline is cleared on success and the body keeps progressing past it.

Focused suite runs (local fallback — Crabbox unavailable in this env):

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run src/media/web-media.test.ts src/media/fetch.test.ts --reporter=verbose

      Tests  121 passed (121)

$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/tlon/src/monitor/media.test.ts extensions/tlon/src/urbit/upload.test.ts --reporter=verbose
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  11 passed (11)
```

### Canonical precedents

- **PR #103020 / merge `26aef8c48bc40d2ea456c2cfc3eca126dca33888`** — `FetchMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs` at `src/media/fetch.ts:82`; the canonical seam. Implements header-only deadline via `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`, `cleanup()`-ed on success so the body is not capped.
- **PR #103266 / merge `541c9f0bf01712d81d5217eb2a5c15d05686259d`** — canonical 15-minute bounded-media ceiling from `src/cli/nodes-camera.ts:20`. This PR reuses the same ceiling on the narrower header-only deadline.
- **Telegram precedent** — `extensions/telegram/src/bot/delivery.resolve-media-retry.ts:356` already uses `TELEGRAM_DOWNLOAD_RESPONSE_HEADER_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000`. This PR's constant names mirror that pattern.

## Coordination with #103209

With the canonical seam now on `origin/main`, both this PR and #103209 independently use that seam — they no longer duplicate each other and either can land in any order. No cross-repo stacking required. Each branch typechecks standalone; the `forwards responseHeaderTimeoutMs from loadWebMediaRaw through readRemoteMediaBuffer` test on this branch and the equivalent proof path on #103209 cover the same end-to-end contract from different call sites (Tlon vs. agent-tools).


## Post-review updates (2026-07-11)

ClawSweeper re-review (2026-07-11 03:40 UTC) identified two P2 findings:

### Stronger forwarding regression test

The original forwarding test created the `Response` synchronously, so headers were already available even if `responseHeaderTimeoutMs` was dropped. Rewrote `src/media/web-media.test.ts > loadWebMedia > forwards responseHeaderTimeoutMs from loadWebMediaRaw through readRemoteMediaBuffer` so the mocked `fetch` delays headers past the configured deadline. If the field is not forwarded, the load remains pending; with correct forwarding, the header deadline fires and the load rejects. Verified by temporarily disabling the forwarding in `src/media/web-media.ts:1004` — the test then fails with `{ status: "pending" }` instead of `{ status: "rejected" }`.

### Removed workstation-specific proof script

Deleted `proof-103206-tool-run.mts`, which contained a non-portable `/media/vdc/OpenClaw/...` import path.

ClawSweeper re-review (2026-07-11 05:28 UTC) identified one P1 finding:

### Removed unused WebMediaOptions expansion

Tlon's `downloadMedia` and `uploadImageFromUrl` call `readRemoteMediaBuffer` and `saveRemoteMedia` directly from `src/media/fetch.ts`, which already accepts `responseHeaderTimeoutMs` in `FetchMediaOptions:82`. The `WebMediaOptions.responseHeaderTimeoutMs` field and `loadWebMediaInternal` forwarding path were unused by the Tlon callers. Removed from `src/media/web-media.ts` (type definition + destructuring + readRemoteMediaBuffer forwarding) and deleted the fake-timer forwarding test from `src/media/web-media.test.ts`.

The Tlon extension changes are unchanged: `downloadMedia` and `uploadImageFromUrl` each define a 15-min local constant and pass `responseHeaderTimeoutMs` directly to the SDK functions that already support it.

target.title: fix(onboard): wait for gateway warnings before installing service
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users completing onboarding through the remote wizard could have Gateway service installation begin before they acknowledged an installation warning.

## Why This Change Was Made

Gateway install-plan warnings are collected synchronously, then displayed and awaited in order before service installation starts. This preserves the install planner's synchronous warning contract while respecting the wizard prompter's asynchronous interaction contract.

## User Impact

Onboarding users now see and acknowledge Gateway installation warnings before OpenClaw installs the service, including when the wizard is driven through the Gateway API.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `402f69a3c0c04f63fe676cf6074b771c8e1dfaa0`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs --testNamePattern "(waits for gateway install warnings before installing the service|shows gateway install warnings when planning fails)" src/wizard/setup.finalize.test.ts` — 2 passed, 25 skipped.
- Current-head remote WizardSession runtime transcript. It runs the production `WizardSession`, onboarding finalizer, and install planner; the Windows service-write and CLI-command boundaries are isolated so no system task is created:

  ```text
  wizard.step installWarning=true
  install_calls_before_ack=0
  wizard.ack installWarning=true
  service.install
  warning_acknowledged_before_service_install=true
  ```

- The planning-failure regression test emits a warning and rejects the plan, then verifies the warning is still shown and service installation is not called.
- `oxfmt --check --threads=1 src/wizard/setup.finalize.ts src/wizard/setup.finalize.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` — passed.
- Branch autoreview against `upstream/main` — no accepted or actionable findings.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the changed production path and regression test and understand the ordering fix.

target.title: feat(stepfun): default to step-3.7-flash
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

PR #88082 added `step-3.7-flash` to both direct StepFun catalogs (`stepfun` and `stepfun-plan`) but left the default model on `step-3.5-flash`. New onboarding runs and catalog defaults still select the older Step 3.5 model instead of the current flagship.

## Why This Change Was Made

`STEPFUN_DEFAULT_MODEL_ID` is the single source for both `STEPFUN_DEFAULT_MODEL_REF` and `STEPFUN_PLAN_DEFAULT_MODEL_REF`. Those refs drive `onboard.ts` `primaryModelRef` and each auth method's `defaultModel`, so flipping the one id repoints both surfaces at `step-3.7-flash` with no other runtime wiring.

## User Impact

- Fresh StepFun onboarding (standard and Step Plan) now defaults to `stepfun/step-3.7-flash` / `stepfun-plan/step-3.7-flash`.
- Existing installs that pinned a model explicitly are unaffected; the change only moves the default for new setups.
- `step-3.5-flash` and `step-3.5-flash-2603` remain selectable.

## Evidence

- `extensions/stepfun/provider-catalog.ts`: `STEPFUN_DEFAULT_MODEL_ID` now `step-3.7-flash`.
- Updated `extensions/stepfun/index.test.ts` default-ref expectations; docs default/alternate wording and config examples updated.
- Local proof (Codex worktree fallback):
  - `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check docs/providers/stepfun.md extensions/stepfun/index.test.ts extensions/stepfun/provider-catalog.ts` — clean.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/stepfun/index.test.ts src/agents/models-config.providers.stepfun.test.ts` — 6 tests passed across 2 shards.


## Fresh-onboarding behavior proof

Drove the real StepFun onboard preset appliers (the functions the setup wizard invokes: `applyStepFunStandardConfig`, `applyStepFunStandardConfigCn`, `applyStepFunPlanConfig`, `applyStepFunPlanConfigCn`) against a fresh empty config. All four fresh auth choices select `step-3.7-flash`:

| Setup                           | `agents.defaults.model.primary` |
|---------------------------------|---------------------------------|
| Standard API key (Global/Intl)  | `stepfun/step-3.7-flash`        |
| Standard API key (China)        | `stepfun/step-3.7-flash`        |
| Step Plan API key (Global/Intl) | `stepfun-plan/step-3.7-flash`   |
| Step Plan API key (China)       | `stepfun-plan/step-3.7-flash`   |

Single shared constant `STEPFUN_DEFAULT_MODEL_ID` repoints both products. Full `openclaw onboard` CLI terminal output was not captured because the local sandbox blocks the package mirror; the appliers above are the exact code the wizard runs to set the primary model.

target.body:
> **Update 2026-07-10 — head `90535b2ea0`: fix ClawSweeper [P2] source-aware plugin compatibility for `read`.** Adding `read` to `DEFAULT_GATEWAY_HTTP_TOOL_DENY` flowed into the plugin loader's `pluginToolDenylist`, so the production plugin resolver dropped a same-named non-optional plugin `read` by name before the final gateway filter — returning 404 even with `hostFsRead` off. Now the deny is **source-aware** (`HOST_FS_BUILTIN_CODING_DENY_NAMES` in `dangerous-tools.ts`): `read` is excluded from the plugin-loader denylist when denied solely by the host-FS default (explicit `gateway.tools.deny`/owner-only/excluded still apply), and the final filter preserves a same-named tool carrying plugin metadata (`getPluginToolMeta`) while the built-in stays gated. Regression test: a plugin `read` stays reachable without a new `gateway.tools.allow` entry. Verified in `node:22-bookworm-slim` arm64 + host toolchain — red/green: reverting the resolver fix makes the new test fail `expected 404 to be 200`; with it, the read-side gate is green (`tools-invoke-http` + `audit` + `schema.help.quality`), `tsgo:core` clean, `oxlint` 1.72 clean.

---

> **Update 2026-07-06 — head `816dd8f5ae`: rebased onto current `main` (now `MERGEABLE`).** Resolved conflicts: `src/security/dangerous-tools.ts` (kept both main's new `computer` deny entry and this PR's `read` entry), `docs/gateway/security/audit-checks.md` (took main's current table + re-inserted the `host_read_allow` row, re-formatted), and `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` (adopted main's refactored budget module + bumped the budgets the new `GatewayDirectInvokeOptIns` public type requires — verified via `plugin-sdk-surface-report --check`). Re-verified in the `node:22-bookworm-slim` arm64 container / host toolchain: read-side gate green (`tools-invoke-http` + `audit-gateway-tools-http` + `schema.help.quality`, 156+23), `tsgo:core` clean, `oxlint` (1.72) clean, `docs-link-audit` 0 broken. No behavior change — same owner-gated `read` opt-in; only conflict resolution + budget/table refresh. The remaining item is maintainer security/product acceptance of the owner-gated host-FS read boundary.

---

> **Update 2026-06-17 — head `d625c6de23` (scope owner gate to built-in host-FS read tool).** Addresses the latest ClawSweeper plugin-fallback finding. The prior wording said a non-owner caller is "refused even when both config keys are set", which overstated the guarantee. Per the resolver (`src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts`), the owner gate scopes **only built-in `read` materialization**: for a non-owner caller the built-in coding tool is not materialized, so a same-named **allowlisted plugin** tool is not gated by `senderIsOwner` and still resolves under the normal `gateway.tools.allow`/`deny` policy. The `hostFsRead` config help (`src/config/schema.help.ts`), the `GatewayDirectInvokeOptIns` `hostFsRead` member comment (`src/config/types.gateway.ts`), the `hostFsRead` bullet in `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md`, and the read section of `docs/gateway/tools-invoke-http-api.md` (prose + truth-table header/rows + a new _Plugin name collision_ note) are now scoped to the built-in tool. Verified in the `node:22-bookworm-slim` linux container: `pnpm check:docs` (format clean, markdownlint 0 errors, MDX ok, 0 broken links) and `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts` (23/23) both green.

> **Update 2026-06-17 — head `7f9876c2b2` (config-help owner-gate sync).** Head moved `ca46eb9946` → `7f9876c2b2` via one commit that extends the owner-gate documentation from the public docs pages into the operator-facing **config help**: the `gateway.tools.directInvoke.hostFsRead` `FIELD_HELP` string (`src/config/schema.help.ts`) and the `GatewayDirectInvokeOptIns` summary + `hostFsRead` member comment (`src/config/types.gateway.ts`) now state the third gate — an owner/admin sender (`senderIsOwner === true`) — instead of describing a two-key surface. Help strings/type comments only; **no runtime code changed** (verified: `git diff ca46eb9946 7f9876c2b2` touches only those two `src/config/*.ts` files, comment/string lines), so the live proof at `5ca72af1ba` below stands unchanged. Verified in the `node:22-bookworm-slim` linux container: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/schema.help.quality.test.ts` (23/23) and `pnpm check:docs` both green.

---

> **Update 2026-06-17 — head `ca46eb9946` (docs-only owner-gate sync).** The head moved `5ca72af1ba` → `ca46eb9946` via a single docs-only commit that brings the operator docs in line with the runtime's three-key gate: the `read` truth table in `docs/gateway/tools-invoke-http-api.md` and the `hostFsRead` bullet in `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md` now carry the **owner/admin sender** column/clause (`senderIsOwner === true`) — matching the triple-key truth table already in this PR description. No source files changed (verified: `git diff 5ca72af1ba ca46eb9946` touches only those two docs files), so `dist/` is byte-identical and the live proof at `5ca72af1ba` below stands unchanged. `pnpm check:docs` passes in the `node:22-bookworm-slim` linux container (format clean, markdownlint 0 errors, MDX ok, 0 broken links).

---

Related to #66561 (orthogonal — direct-invoke read benefits the embedded run-budget cascade but does not fix the underlying SSE timeout it describes; that issue should remain open). Narrow first landing of the broader direct-invoke umbrella tracked in #37131.

## Summary

Wire the `read` coding tool into the gateway direct-invoke surfaces (HTTP `POST /tools/invoke` AND SDK RPC `tools.invoke`, which share the resolver) so it is reachable for deterministic automation — CI/preflight checks, lint pipelines, browser capture flows — without an LLM round-trip.

**This PR is the redesigned narrow read-only landing.** Rebased onto current upstream `023ce6e96c38`. The exposure of `read` is now behind **triple-key gating** so neither the existing `gateway.tools.allow: ["read"]` knob nor the new opt-in silently grants host-FS read, and a non-owner trusted-proxy caller can never reach it.

## Triple-key gating (addresses ClawSweeper [P1] + owner hardening)

To reach `read` on the direct-invoke surface, ALL THREE must hold:

| Key | Purpose | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `gateway.tools.allow: ["read"]` | Lifts `read` from `DEFAULT_GATEWAY_HTTP_TOOL_DENY` (now extended with `"read"`). Existing knob; keeps the operator-acceptance step visible in the standard policy surface. | not present |
| `gateway.tools.directInvoke.hostFsRead: true` | **NEW.** Distinct surface-specific opt-in. Without this, `read` is not materialized into the candidate set even if `tools.allow` includes it. | `false` (omitted) |
| `senderIsOwner === true` | **NEW owner gate.** Host-filesystem read is materialized only for an owner/admin sender. A trusted-proxy `operator.write` caller is denied even with both config keys set. | n/a (per-request) |

**Any key alone (or any two) leaves `read` unreachable.** Old configs that already contain `allow: ["read"]` for unrelated reasons (e.g. an MCP/agent surface where `read` was always available) stay inert at the direct-invoke layer — no silent upgrade-time expansion — and even a fully-opted-in config refuses non-owner callers.

| `tools.allow` ⊇ `"read"` | `directInvoke.hostFsRead` | sender is owner | `read` reachable on direct-invoke |
|---|---|---|---|
| no  | no   | —   | ❌ |
| yes | no   | yes | ❌ (tool not materialized) |
| no  | yes  | yes | ❌ (filtered by HTTP deny) |
| yes | yes  | **no**  | ❌ (**owner gate**) |
| yes | yes  | yes | ✅ |

## Scope

- **Read-only.** Mutating coding primitives (`write` / `edit` / `apply_patch` / `exec` / `process`) are NOT exposed by this PR.
- **Both surfaces.** Gating applies to HTTP `POST /tools/invoke` AND the SDK-facing JSON-RPC `tools.invoke` (they share `resolveGatewayScopedTools`).
- **MCP loopback unaffected.** `surface === "loopback"` is not gated.
- **Hook-bypass safe.** Uses new `createOpenClawCodingToolsRaw` export (module-private Symbol marker, not reachable from typed SDK params) so HTTP-surface tools aren't double-wrapped — `handleToolsInvokeHttp` already runs `runBeforeToolCallHook` itself before dispatch.

## Files changed

- `src/agents/agent-tools.ts` — `SKIP_BEFORE_TOOL_CALL_HOOK` symbol + `createOpenClawCodingToolsRaw` export
- `src/config/types.gateway.ts` — `GatewayToolsConfig.directInvoke: GatewayDirectInvokeOptIns` field (new type)
- `src/security/dangerous-tools.ts` — `"read"` added to `DEFAULT_GATEWAY_HTTP_TOOL_DENY`
- `src/gateway/tool-resolution.ts` — triple-key gated materialization of `read` into the candidate set (`tools.allow` ∋ read AND `directInvoke.hostFsRead` AND `senderIsOwner`)
- `src/gateway/tools-invoke-http.test.ts` — real-transport owner/non-owner cases on HTTP `/tools/invoke` and RPC `tools.invoke`
- `src/security/audit-gateway-config.ts` — `gateway.tools_invoke_http.host_read_allow` finding (only fires when the config gates are set; silent otherwise since `read` is unreachable there)
- `src/security/audit-gateway-tools-http.test.ts` — test cases covering all gate combinations + vanilla
- `docs/gateway/tools-invoke-http-api.md` — operator-facing opt-in docs with config example + truth table
- `scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` — `+1` surface-budget bump (4 dimensions) to admit the single new `GatewayDirectInvokeOptIns` public config type; no runtime impact

## Why a redesigned commit history (not a rebase of the prior 10)

The original PR's commits implemented an OLD design (single-key `allow: ["read"]` as the opt-in). The bot's P1 — "Require a fresh opt-in before enabling host reads" — needed a fundamentally different shape, not patches on top. Plus the prior commits referenced `src/agents/pi-tools.ts` which has been renamed to `src/agents/agent-tools.ts` upstream. The branch was reset onto upstream and the redesign written cleanly, then rebased again onto current upstream `023ce6e96c38`. Backup of pre-rebase history retained at `backup/read-only-pre-rebase-120fd2` on the public fork.

The final commit (`chore(plugin-sdk): bump surface budgets +1 for GatewayDirectInvokeOptIns`) is the only behavioural-neutral addition: the new public config type `GatewayDirectInvokeOptIns` adds exactly one top-level export, which the `plugin-sdk-surface-report --check` budget ratchet (run by `checks-node-core-fast`) counts against four dimensions (`config-types`, public exports, public function exports, public deprecated exports — the monolithic `config-types` entrypoint is `@deprecated`). Each budget constant is bumped `+1` to admit the single new type; no runtime code is touched by that commit, so the live proof and `dist/` are identical with or without it.

---

## Real behavior proof

> **Head `5ca72af1ba`** — rebased onto current upstream `023ce6e96c38` (the prior base `120fd2f702` was 28 commits stale; upstream `1c0b38f960 fix(sdk): refresh plugin surface baselines` is included in the new base). Re-built and re-proven from scratch in docker at this exact head. CI verified locally before push (in `node:22-bookworm-slim` arm64): oxlint (3 shards, 0/0), `tsgo:core` (0), `tsgo:test` / `check:test-types` (0), `plugin-sdk-surface-report` vitest (4/4), and the 3 PR-touched test files 143/143 (7 file-projects).

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Expose the `read` coding tool over Gateway direct-invoke surfaces (HTTP `POST /tools/invoke` AND SDK RPC `tools.invoke`, which share the resolver) for deterministic automation, gated behind `gateway.tools.allow: ["read"]` + the NEW `gateway.tools.directInvoke.hostFsRead: true` opt-in + an owner gate. Addresses ClawSweeper [P1] (legacy single-key config must NOT silently grant host-FS read on upgrade) and adds owner-only enforcement so a non-owner trusted-proxy caller is refused even when both config keys are set.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** built `dist/` + `packages/sdk/dist/` inside the container at head `5ca72af1ba`, then `PROOF_HEAD=5ca72af1bab7ad9d06136c47861c5d087f4d5a71 bash .proof-85664.sh` — runs a live gateway per case over a real socket. 6 cases: HTTP trusted-proxy surface (owner=`operator.admin`, non-owner=`operator.write`) for cases 1–5; SDK `GatewayClientTransport` shared-secret bearer (= owner) for case 6.

**Real environment tested:** built fresh from head `5ca72af1bab7ad9d06136c47861c5d087f4d5a71` inside `node:22-bookworm-slim` arm64-native container (pnpm v11.2.2, linux-arm64 packages in a named volume). Gateway started per case via `openclaw gateway run`; each case dispatched via real HTTP `POST /tools/invoke` and (case 6) the SDK `GatewayClientTransport` WebSocket `oc.tools.invoke(...)`. Unit tests in the same container: 143/143 passing (7 files), including the real-transport owner/non-owner cases on the `gateway-server` and `gateway-client` projects.

**Evidence after fix (terminal capture, head `5ca72af1ba`):** from the `node:22-bookworm-slim` (linux/arm64) container:

```
=== HEAD: 5ca72af1bab7 ===

### LIVE PROOF (HTTP trusted-proxy surface) ###

--- 1 R-OWNER-ENABLED   (allow=[read] hostFsRead=true, operator.admin) ---
  [HTTP operator.admin] 200 {"ok":true,"result":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"PROOF READ SENTINEL at 5ca72af1bab7\\n"}]}}
--- 2 R-NONOWNER-DENIED (allow=[read] hostFsRead=true, operator.write) ---
  [HTTP operator.write] 404 {"ok":false,"error":{"type":"not_found","message":"Tool not available: read"}}

--- 3 R-DENIED-no-opt-in (allow=[read] hostFsRead=false, operator.admin) ---
  [HTTP operator.admin] 404 {"ok":false,"error":{"type":"not_found","message":"Tool not available: read"}}

--- 4 R-DENIED-no-allow  (allow=[] hostFsRead=true, operator.admin) ---
  [HTTP operator.admin] 404 {"ok":false,"error":{"type":"not_found","message":"Tool not available: read"}}

--- 5 WRITE-still-denied (allow=[write] hostFsRead=true, operator.admin, tool=write) ---
  [HTTP operator.admin] 404 {"ok":false,"error":{"type":"not_found","message":"Tool not available: write"}}

### LIVE PROOF (SDK token surface — shared-secret bearer = owner) ###

--- 6 SDK-OWNER-ENABLED (allow=[read] hostFsRead=true, token bearer) ---
  [SDK token] {"ok":true,"toolName":"read","output":{"content":[{"type":"text","text":"PROOF READ SENTINEL at 5ca72af1bab7\\n"}]},"source":"core"}

=== PROOF COMPLETE: HEAD=5ca72af1bab7 ===
=== UNIT TESTS ===
 Test Files  7 passed (7)
      Tests  143 passed (143)
```

**Observed result after fix (head `5ca72af1ba`):**
- **Case 1 R-OWNER-ENABLED** — all three keys satisfied (owner `operator.admin`, both config keys) → HTTP 200 with the actual sentinel file content.
- **Case 2 R-NONOWNER-DENIED** — both config keys set but caller is `operator.write` (non-owner) → 404. **This is the owner gate working**: a trusted-proxy non-owner cannot reach host read even with the opt-in fully enabled.
- **Case 3 R-DENIED-no-opt-in** — `allow:["read"]` but `hostFsRead:false`, owner → 404 (P1 fix: legacy config stays inert).
- **Case 4 R-DENIED-no-allow** — `hostFsRead:true` but `allow:[]`, owner → 404 (both config keys required).
- **Case 5 WRITE-still-denied** — `allow:["write"]`, `hostFsRead:true`, owner, tool=`write` → 404 (read-only scope confirmed; the opt-in does not leak to mutating tools).
- **Case 6 SDK-OWNER-ENABLED** — SDK RPC `tools.invoke` over a shared-secret bearer (always owner) with both config keys → `ok:true`, `source:"core"`, same sentinel content. Confirms the SDK surface shares the resolver and the same gate.

**What was not tested:** Write/edit/exec/process are out of scope for this read-only PR (write/edit covered by #63919). `apply_patch` is in the deny list, not yet factory-produced. SDK over trusted-proxy WS additionally requires device pairing ("device identity required"), so the SDK non-owner path is covered by the shared `gateway-client` unit test rather than a live SDK socket; the resolver under test is identical across surfaces.

## Docs discoverability

Addresses ClawSweeper's [P2]: "Document the host-FS read opt-in everywhere."

- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — FIELD_HELP entries for `gateway.tools.directInvoke` and `gateway.tools.directInvoke.hostFsRead`.
- `docs/gateway/configuration-reference.md` — paragraph describing the gating + audit warning hookup.
- `docs/gateway/security/audit-checks.md` — catalog row for `gateway.tools_invoke_http.host_read_allow` with severity, criteria, and config-key references.

So operators using config help/lookup or security-audit docs can discover this security-sensitive opt-in and warning.

target.title: fix(clickclack): add timeouts to REST client requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users relying on the ClickClack plugin could have sends, message fetches, or activity REST calls wait indefinitely when the ClickClack API accepted the request or sent headers but then stalled the response body.

## Why This Change Was Made

The ClickClack REST client now applies an owner-local 30s request deadline with the shared OpenClaw timeout helper, preserves any caller-provided abort signal, and keeps the deadline active until success and error response bodies finish reading. This keeps the existing WebSocket path and FormData upload semantics unchanged and does not add new config or environment surface.

## User Impact

ClickClack REST operations now fail quickly with a timeout instead of leaving gateway startup, inbound message lookup, outbound delivery, or activity writes stuck on a network black hole. Existing callers keep the same API behavior unless the remote service stops responding within the deadline.

## Evidence

Base: upstream/main `3ec2a50d6c0a62a484e630536c658a8357e4e211`
Head: `8b56e17920` (`fix(clickclack): add timeouts to REST client requests`)

- `node scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs warmup --provider blacksmith-testbox --keep --timing-json` - blocked before remote execution: selected `crabbox` binary failed basic `--version`/`--help` sanity checks.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts` - passed after rebasing to latest upstream/main, 1 file / 16 tests.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/clickclack/src/inbound.test.ts extensions/clickclack/src/gateway.test.ts extensions/clickclack/src/activity.test.ts extensions/clickclack/src/session-route.test.ts extensions/clickclack/src/accounts.test.ts extensions/clickclack/src/outbound.test.ts extensions/clickclack/src/target.test.ts extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts` - passed before the latest rebase, 8 files / 63 tests.
- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental false --pretty false` - passed before the latest rebase.
- `oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.ts extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts` - passed after rebasing to latest upstream/main.
- `oxlint --threads=1 extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.ts extensions/clickclack/src/http-client.test.ts` - passed after rebasing to latest upstream/main.
- `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` - passed after rebasing to latest upstream/main.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode branch --base upstream/main --engine claude` - clean, no accepted/actionable findings before the latest rebase; the rebase was conflict-free and only moved the same patch onto latest main.

Note: `node scripts/test-extension.mjs clickclack` resolved the expected 8 ClickClack test files but could not complete in this isolated worktree because pnpm attempted a dependency-status install/removal of the temporary `node_modules` link in a no-TTY session. The same 8 files were run through `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` with the repository extension Vitest config instead.


### Native Fetch Controlled-Server Timeout Proof (2026-07-11)

Head: `8b56e17920b438252d76cbe381ab6d97f248c808`.

The server returns a normal `/api/me` response, then accepts `POST /api/channels/proof-channel/messages`, sends response headers, and stalls the response body.

target.title: fix(slack): use endsWith instead of includes for _all_ action_id matching
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`isBulkActionsBlock()` used substring `includes("_all_")` to detect bulk-action rows. That heuristic is unsafe:

1. **False positives**: IDs like `deploy_all_services` contain `_all_` and were incorrectly removed during confirmation updates.
2. **No producer contract**: bare `select_all` / `deselect_all` were never namespaced and global suffix rules reserve unrelated IDs.

## Changes

- Add a **private** Slack bulk contract in `extensions/slack/src/bulk-action-ids.ts` (not exported from `api.ts`):
  - preferred producer marker: `block_id` prefix `openclaw:bulk:`
  - preferred action IDs: `openclaw:bulk:select_all`, `openclaw:bulk:deselect_all`
  - immutable internal ID collections (no mutable exported `Set`)
  - internal producer helper: `buildOpenClawBulkActionsBlock()`
- `interactions.block-actions.ts`: classify bulk rows via `isSlackBulkActionsBlock()`:
  - OpenClaw marker + closed IDs (new producers)
  - legacy bare `select_all` / `deselect_all` pair only (upgrade compatibility)
  - **no** global `_all` suffix and **no** `deploy_all_services` false positives
- Add grammar, legacy-upgrade, and whole-path handler regressions.

## Upgrade contract

| Producer shape | Bulk cleanup |
|---|---|
| `openclaw:bulk:*` block + closed action IDs | yes (preferred) |
| bare `select_all` + `deselect_all` row | yes (legacy compatibility) |
| `deploy_all_services` / `archive_all` / substring `_all_` heuristics | no (intentional fix) |

## Evidence

**Current head:** `d1cac6ab`

**Unit tests:**
```
pnpm test extensions/slack/src/bulk-action-ids.test.ts
pnpm test extensions/slack/src/monitor/events/interactions.test.ts -t "bulk|deploy_all_services|legacy bare"
→ 16 passed
```

**Live Slack proof (redacted, workspace channel `C0BGQ1REJ3T`):**

1. **Bulk row removed when last individual control is selected** — message ts `1783746112.698819`
2. **`deploy_all_services` preserved when another individual row remains** — message ts `1783746090.752499`

**Lint:** oxlint on touched files — clean

## Review

- ClawSweeper gold follow-up addressed: removed speculative public API exports, made ID collections private/immutable, documented legacy upgrade boundary
- AI-assisted: Yes

target.title: refactor(gateway): centralize agent wait lifecycle
target.body:
Closes #104135

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves an internal Gateway reliability problem where `agent.wait` reconciled two independent terminal-state owners: lifecycle observations in the agent job cache and terminal Gateway dedupe entries. Each path maintained its own waiter machinery, and the RPC handler raced both promises before deciding which result won.

## Why This Change Was Made

The agent job registry now ingests both lifecycle and dedupe terminal observations, applies the existing canonical terminal-outcome precedence, and owns the only waiter registry. A closed source tag preserves the existing active-chat/run-ID collision behavior. The separate dedupe wait module, handler-level `Promise.race`, and dead cancellation path are removed.

## User Impact

No intended user-visible behavior change. Agent waits now have one deterministic terminal-state owner, while Gateway event fan-out no longer registers one global agent-event listener per waiter.

## Evidence

- Blacksmith Testbox: 224 focused Gateway tests passed; targeted type-aware lint passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox: 744 broader Gateway tests passed; core and core-test `tsgo` lanes passed. The environment stopped externally during later full-core lint stripes, so no full `check:changed` claim is made.
- Exact-head path gate: core and core-test type lanes, targeted lint, conflict/dependency guards, database-first guard, runtime loader/cycle guards, and pairing/webhook guards passed.
- GitHub CI on the previous head commit: build artifacts, core lint, production/test types, and the relevant compact Node shard passed. Both QA Smoke failures reproduce on exact `origin/main` and stop before scenarios because the current release changelog section is missing.
- Collision repair proof: focused disagreement tests cover older sticky cancellation/timeout state followed by a newer cross-source completion, plus fresh lifecycle completion after a dedupe snapshot.
- Ephemeral Gateway proof on the exact head commit: full production build, isolated onboarding and state, real Gateway process, normal CLI agent turn, direct agent RPC with two concurrent waits plus a cached wait, and UI-style `chat.send` with two concurrent waits plus a cached wait.
- Runtime completion proof: three mocked provider requests completed, every wait finished `ok`, the Gateway remained healthy afterward, and logs contained no crash markers.
- Runtime timeout proof: a mocked provider accepted the request and intentionally did not respond. Two concurrent waits and a cached wait all returned a terminal timeout; the Gateway remained healthy afterward and logs contained no crash markers.
- Ephemeral environments were stopped after verification.

target.title: fix(signal): surface daemon errors split across output chunks
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Signal operators running the auto-started `signal-cli` daemon could have an error line split across stdout or stderr chunks and forwarded as ordinary log fragments instead of one error diagnostic.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared Signal daemon output boundary now reads complete lines before applying the existing log classifier. This covers both stdout and stderr, preserves CRLF and LF input plus a final unterminated line, and does not change daemon lifecycle, configuration, or channel delivery behavior.

## User Impact

Signal daemon failures remain visible at the error level even when the operating system splits one log line across multiple stream chunks.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: real `signal-cli` daemon stderr split across child-process chunks is reconstructed before severity classification, so one daemon failure produces one error-level record.
- Current head: `9ea914269198d773adabe2a896ba16e4a78d3b06`.
- Real-daemon setup: OpenClaw's `spawnSignalDaemon` launched the official JVM release `signal-cli 0.14.5` in multi-account mode with an empty temporary data directory and no Signal account. The configured HTTP port was deliberately occupied so the real daemon emitted `Failed to initialize HTTP Server`. A byte-preserving relay limited stderr writes to at most 2 characters, forcing that diagnostic across child-process chunk boundaries.
- Redacted terminal transcript:

  ```text
  signal-cli version: signal-cli 0.14.5
  transport fault: stderr relayed in writes of at most 2 characters
  matching error-level records: 1
  signal-cli: Failed to initialize HTTP Server
  ```

- Focused regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/daemon.test.ts` passed all 5 tests.
- Targeted format: `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/signal/src/daemon.ts extensions/signal/src/daemon.test.ts` passed.
- Diff hygiene: `git diff --check HEAD~1..HEAD` passed.
- Autoreview: `python .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` completed with no accepted/actionable findings.

target.title: test(plugins): cover filtered bundle MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text
Proof root: /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins install --link /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp
Linked plugin path: /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp
Restart the gateway to load plugins.
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins inspect vision-mcp --json
{
  "diagnostics": [],
  "command": "npx",
  "args": [
    "-y",
    "@vision-mcp/cli@latest",
    "serve",
    "--apps-root",
    "/private/var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp/apps"
  ],
  "cwdEndsWith": true,
  "toolFilter": {
    "include": [
      "capsule.*",
      "vision_map.snapshot",
      "vision_map.list_apps",
      "vision_map.list_workflows",
      "vision_map.describe_workflow",
      "vision_map.describe",
      "vision_map.detect_state",
      "vision_map.list_actions",
      "vision_map.describe_action",
      "vision_map.perform_action",
      "vision_map.run_workflow",
      "vision_map.verify",
      "vision_map.repair_minimal",
      "vision_map.export_trace"
    ],
    "exclude": [
      "vision_map.click_at",
      "vision_map.type_text",
      "vision_map.press_key",
      "vision_map.scroll",
      "vision_map.init",
      "vision_map.apply_patch",
      "vision_map.add_control",
      "vision_map.commit_*",
      "vision_map.harvest_session"
    ]
  }
}
```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

Regression coverage added: `src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts` now covers a Codex-compatible bundle MCP config with a filtered server and a relative `./apps` data root.

Validation results:

```text
src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: 1 file passed, 8 tests passed
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: All matched files use the correct format
git diff --check: passed
pnpm check:docs: Docs formatting clean; markdownlint 0 errors; MDX check passed; i18n glossary passed; checked_internal_links=4554; broken_links=0
codex review --base origin/main: No actionable correctness issues were found
```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

AI-assisted: yes.

Next action: maintainer review.

target.title: docs(memory): align descriptors and docs with recursive memory/**/*.md
target.body:
## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```
$ openclaw memory status
Memory Search (main)
Provider: local (requested: local)
Sources: memory
Extra paths: ~/.openclaw/shared-memory
Indexed: 105/105 files . 933 chunks
Workspace: ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku
By source:
  memory . 105/105 files . 933 chunks
```

```
$ openclaw memory index
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
Memory index updated (main).
```

```
$ openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
[node-llama-cpp] ... falling back to using no GPU
0.812 memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md:1-9
    Recursive memory search proof.
    Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
    This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
    to verify that nested dated memory files are indexed and searchable
    by the runtime.

0.450 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md:1-6
0.432 memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/pr-draft.md:1-32
```

After-patch text observed from this branch (HEAD `30f15f4e22`) by importing the modified modules at runtime:

```
$ node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs
=== schema.help.ts: FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch'] ===
Vector search over MEMORY.md and memory/**/*.md (per-agent overrides supported).

=== prompt-section.ts: buildPromptSection({ memory_search + memory_get }) ===
    [section header line: "## Memory Recall"]
    Before answering anything about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos: run memory_search on MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md + indexed session transcripts; then use memory_get to pull only the needed lines. If low confidence after search, say you checked.
    Citations are disabled: do not mention file paths or line numbers in replies unless the user explicitly asks.

=== prompt-section.ts: buildPromptSection({ memory_search only }) ===
    [section header line: "## Memory Recall"]
    Before answering anything about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos: run memory_search on MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md + indexed session transcripts and answer from the matching results. If low confidence after search, say you checked.
    Citations are disabled: do not mention file paths or line numbers in replies unless the user explicitly asks.

=== extensions/memory-core/index.ts (post-patch source lines) ===
 127      description:
 128        "Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. ...",

 139      description:
 140        "Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/**/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.",

=== extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts (post-patch source lines) ===
 240      description:
 241        "Mandatory recall step: semantically search MEMORY.md + memory/**/*.md (and optional session transcripts) before answering questions about prior work, decisions, dates, people, preferences, or todos. ...",

 410      description:
 411        "Safe exact excerpt read from MEMORY.md or memory/**/*.md. Defaults to a bounded excerpt when lines are omitted, includes truncation/continuation info when more content exists, and `corpus=wiki` reads from registered compiled-wiki supplements.",
```

**Observed result after fix**: (a) The freshly written nested file `memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md` (two levels deep under `memory/`) was indexed by `openclaw memory index` and returned as the top match (score `0.812`) for the unique token. A second nested hit from `memory/fix-openclaw/memory-recursive-search/smoke/2026-04-27.md` (three levels deep) confirms recursion is not limited to one level. (b) Importing the modified `FIELD_HELP` map and `buildPromptSection` from this branch at runtime shows the after-patch strings carry `memory/**/*.md` for both the config help text and the system-prompt memory recall guidance, matching the diff exactly. (c) The two `memory_search` / `memory_get` description strings in `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` and `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` are inline string literals; the after-patch lines printed from this branch show the new wording in place. No runtime code paths are modified, only the descriptor and doc strings plus the regenerated `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256`.

**What was not tested**: This PR does not introduce or modify any runtime code path, so additional behavior tests beyond the search smoke above were not added. The recursive walk itself (`collectMemoryFilesFromDir`) is already covered by upstream tests under `packages/memory-host-sdk/`.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm config:docs:gen` regenerates baseline cleanly (no other drift)
- [x] Nested memory smoke search on installed `2026.5.20` returns the new nested file at score `0.812`
- [x] On-branch runtime import shows `FIELD_HELP['agents.defaults.memorySearch']`, `buildPromptSection(...)` output, and `memory_search` / `memory_get` description literals all carry `memory/**/*.md`
- [ ] CI: lint / type / config-baseline check

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text

    "include": [
      "capsule.*",

    ],
    "exclude": [
      "vision_map.click_at",

```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

Regression coverage added: `src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts` now covers a Codex-compatible bundle MCP config with a filtered server and a relative `./apps` data root.

Validation results:

```text
src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: 1 file passed, 8 tests passed
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: All matched files use the correct format
git diff --check: passed
pnpm check:docs: Docs formatting clean; markdownlint 0 errors; MDX check passed; i18n glossary passed; checked_internal_links=4554; broken_links=0
codex review --base origin/main: No actionable correctness issues were found
```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

AI-assisted: yes.

## Summary

- Problem: new Control UI dashboard sessions without a label/displayName fall back to raw session keys, making multiple new chats hard to distinguish.
- Solution: add a Control UI fallback that renders unnamed dashboard sessions as their local creation time.
- What changed: gateway session rows now expose `sessionStartedAt`; Control UI uses it for dashboard-session display fallback, with `updatedAt` as a legacy fallback.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no persisted labels are written, no rename UI was added, and explicit labels/display names still win.

AI-assisted: yes. I used a local coding agent and ran the verification below myself.

## Motivation

- Closes #86040.
- This is a low-friction UX improvement for users who create several dashboard chats with `/NEW` and need to pick the right session at a glance.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
